name: Aberdare
intro: In the 2021 Census, 8.4% of working residents in the Aberdare built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, nearly double the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and that census was taken during a lockdown. Long runs out of the Cynon Valley are where Stage 1 remapping on a diesel makes the most difference day to day. The remap changes the fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine software, inside the limits the engine was built for. The result is more torque through the mid-range, so the car keeps its pace on climbs and on faster roads with fewer gear changes, and acceleration feels more responsive.
driving: Mountain Ash is 4.7 km from Aberdare, Merthyr Tydfil 6.7 km and Rhondda 7.7 km. The A465, A470 and A4059 are among the main roads around the town, and the nearest service area is Sarn Park on the M4, 21.5 km away. Most working residents of the built-up area, 61.9%, drove to work at the 2021 Census, against 45.1% across England and Wales. The Rhondda Cynon Taf council area had 106 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, below the Wales figure of 117. In 2025 MOT tests across CF postcodes, the Ford Transit Custom was the third most tested diesel van. Loaded, a Transit Custom gains steadier pulling from Stage 1.

name: Aberdeen

caz.name: Aberdeen Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers the city centre and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Privately kept diesel cars in the Aberdeen City council area fell from 22,077 to 19,715 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 10.7%. That is the steepest fall of the 104 largest towns we cover, and diesel is now 21.3% of private cars there, against 63.5% on petrol. If you are keeping your diesel rather than replacing it, Stage 1 remapping is one way to get more from the engine you already have. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. The gain most diesel drivers notice is mid-range torque: easier overtaking, smoother joins onto faster roads and fewer downshifts.
driving: The Aberdeen Low Emission Zone covers the city centre and applies to both cars and vans, enforced by a penalty charge rather than a fee to enter. A remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it makes no difference to whether the zone applies to yours. The A96, A92, A93 and A944 are among the main roads, and the nearest service area, Stracathro on the A90, is 51.5 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across AB postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Land Rover Discovery were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter. For a Discovery with a trailer or a loaded Transit on a long A-road run, extra mid-range torque is what you feel.

name: Abingdon-on-Thames
intro: Plug-in cars made up 7.1% of privately kept cars in the Vale of White Horse council area at the end of June 2026, above the England figure of 5.3%. Even so, diesel was still 28.6% and petrol 57%, so most cars in the council area that includes Abingdon-on-Thames still run on a combustion engine, and that engine is what Stage 1 remapping works on. The remap changes fuel, boost and timing settings in software, kept within the engine's limits, and leaves the hardware as it is. On a diesel you feel it as stronger mid-range torque, which helps when merging onto the A34 or pulling a trailer. A vehicle with a fault, such as a blocked DPF or a failing injector, has it put right before the remap.
driving: Eight A roads appear on the list for Abingdon-on-Thames, the A34 and A420 among them, but no motorway. Oxford, 8.8 km off, and Didcot, at 7.7 km, are the nearest towns, and Witney is 18.8 km away. Peartree Services on the A44 is 13 km away and Welcome Break Oxford on the M40 14 km. Most commutes were local in the 2021 Census, taken in a lockdown: 14.6% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more, against 20.7% across the Vale of White Horse council area and 19% for England and Wales. Among diesel vans at OX postcode MOT stations in 2025, the Ford Transit Connect made the top five, and a remap makes a fully loaded Transit Connect less of a struggle on the A34.

name: Accrington
intro: Five towns lie within 8 km of Accrington: Oswaldtwistle at 2.7 km, Great Harwood at 5.1 km, then Padiham, Haslingden and Rawtenstall. On trips that short, what you notice from Stage 1 remapping is the response in the lower gears, not anything at motorway speed: a diesel pulls more willingly out of junctions and up hills without dropping a gear. The settings for fuel, boost and timing are changed in software, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Any change in fuel use is small and depends on how you drive, and the M65 is there when a longer run calls on the extra mid-range.
driving: Vans are more common in Hyndburn than across England. The Hyndburn council area had 94 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 for England, and 96.6% of those vans ran on diesel. In BB postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter was the second most tested diesel van in 2025 MOT tests, after the Ford Transit. Loaded vans like these gain most from extra low-rev torque, within the limits of the clutch and gearbox. At the 2021 Census, 30% of households in the Accrington built-up area had no car, against 23.3% for England and Wales, while 56.5% of working residents drove to work. ExtraMSA Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 8.7 km away.

name: Airdrie
intro: Five neighbouring towns lie within 10 km of Airdrie, from Coatbridge at 3.9 km to Cumbernauld at 9.4 km, with Bellshill, Viewpark and Motherwell in between. Local trips can be short, and the M8 is on the town's road list for longer ones. Stage 1 remapping is aimed at both kinds of driving. More mid-range torque on a diesel means fewer gear changes at low speed and a firmer pull when merging with motorway traffic. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, and the engine itself is left as it is.
driving: RoadChef Bothwell Services on the M74 is 8.1 km away, RoadChef Hamilton Services 9.6 km and Heart of Scotland Services 13.2 km. The A73 and A89 are among the A roads on the list. Few residents commute far: in Scotland's 2022 Census, 2.8% of working residents in the Airdrie locality travelled 30 km or more, under the 4.9% for Scotland, while 50.8% drove to work. Diesel made up 27.4% of privately kept cars in the North Lanarkshire council area at the end of June 2026, close to the Scotland figure of 27.7%. In 2025 MOT tests across ML postcodes, the Ford Focus was the most tested diesel car, an everyday car where a remap mainly brings easier mid-range pull.

name: Aldershot
intro: Four places lie within 5.1 km of Aldershot: Ash and Ash Vale at 2.3 km, Weybourne at 2.9 km, Farnborough at 4.2 km and Farnham at 5.1 km. With neighbours that close, a lot of local driving is likely to be short trips, pulling away from junctions again and again. That is where a diesel's response from low revs gets noticed, and it is the part of the rev range Stage 1 remapping works on. The extra torque means the car picks up more cleanly and needs fewer gear changes in traffic. The remap is a software change to fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside the engine's limits, with no extra parts. Insurers must be told about it once it is done.
driving: No motorway appears among Aldershot's main roads, which include the A331, A31, A323 and A325. The nearest service area is Welcome Break Fleet on the M3, 8.8 km away, with Liphook on the A3 at 18.9 km. At the 2021 Census, taken in a lockdown, 21.8% of working residents in the Aldershot built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% for England and Wales, and 5.4% went 30 km or more, against 4.4%. Diesel made up 26.4% of privately kept cars in the Rushmoor council area at the end of June 2026. At GU postcode MOT stations in 2025, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, and on a Golf, Stage 1 makes joining the A331 or overtaking on the A31 easier.

name: Altrincham
intro: Tabley Hill, Knutsford and Lymm, all service areas on the M6, are between 10.4 km and 11.1 km from Altrincham. The town's own road list adds the M56 and M60, so many longer runs from here are likely to include motorway miles, and joining and overtaking at motorway speed is where a Stage 1 remap on a diesel is most noticeable. No hardware is involved, just the engine's own fuel, boost and timing settings, adjusted within its limits. The extra mid-range torque shows up as easier overtaking and fewer downshifts once you are up to speed. Insurers must be told about a remap, so it is worth speaking to yours before booking.
driving: Sale is 3.5 km from Altrincham, Hale 4.8 km and Wythenshawe 4.9 km, and addresses carry both WA and M postcodes: WA14, WA15, M33 and M23. In the 2021 Census, only 16.1% of households in the Altrincham built-up area had no car, below the Trafford council area's 19.3% and well below the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. In the Trafford council area at the end of June 2026, 6.1% of privately kept cars were plug-ins and 8.9% were petrol hybrids, both above England's 5.3% and 7.7%. The Ford Kuga and Ford Focus were the most tested diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across WA postcodes, and on family diesels like these a remap mostly means more relaxed overtaking and towing.

name: Andover
intro: Long commutes stand out in Andover's 2021 Census figures: 7.5% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales and 6.4% across the Test Valley council area. That was on a census day during a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual. Regular long runs are where a Stage 1 remap is felt most often. On a diesel it lifts mid-range torque, which makes overtaking and joining faster roads easier and cuts the number of downshifts on long climbs. The change is to fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits. Economy gains, if any, are modest and depend on your driving.
driving: All three service areas on Andover's list sit on the A303: Weyhill at 4.1 km, The Buck at 5.2 km and Barton Stacey at 7.7 km. The A3057, A3093, A342 and A343 complete the main roads. Tidworth, the nearest town on the list, is 13.8 km off. In the Test Valley council area, 30.1% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, slightly above England's 29.1%, and there were 87 private vans per 1,000 private cars, against 81. At SP postcode MOT stations in 2025, 44.9% of the cars and small vans tested were diesel, and the Volkswagen Transporter was second only to the Ford Transit among diesel vans. A Transporter loaded for a run on the A303 needs fewer downshifts after a remap.

name: Antrim

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021, during a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual. NISRA settlement figures are approximated from small areas; workers exclude full-time students, and distance bands count work within Northern Ireland only.

intro: For 29.9% of working residents in the Antrim settlement, the trip to work in the 2021 Census was 10 km or more, against 25.6% across Northern Ireland. That count only covers work within Northern Ireland, and census day fell in a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual. With the M2 and M22 both on the town's road list, Stage 1 remapping makes most sense for a commuter's diesel at motorway pace, where more mid-range torque means overtaking without working the engine hard. Nothing is bolted on: the change is made to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within its limits.
driving: Temple Patrick Services on the M2 is 12.7 km from Antrim, Lisburn Services on the M1 25.2 km and Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 35.7 km. The town sits on the north-east shore of Lough Neagh, and the A6, A26, A57 and A522 are among its other main roads. Ballyclare is 14.1 km off and Ballymena 16.8 km. In the 2021 Census, 63.8% of working residents drove to work, a little above the Northern Ireland figure of 62.7%, while 22.9% of households had no car or van, against 19.5%. Across the Antrim and Newtownabbey council area, 43.4% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, below Northern Ireland's 52.7%. A car with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired before any remap.

name: Arnold
intro: Only 12.4% of working residents in the Arnold built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, against 19% across England and Wales. The count was taken during a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual, but it still points to short, local journeys for many people. Short trips are where a diesel's low-rev response matters most, pulling away and working up through the gears. Stage 1 remapping changes the fuel, boost and timing settings in software, inside the engine's limits, to give more torque in that range. One thing comes first: if the car shows a DPF or EGR warning, the fault is repaired before any remap.
driving: In the Gedling council area, diesel made up 29.2% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, just above England's 29.1%, and plug-in cars 5.7%. The A60 and A614 are among Arnold's main roads, with the A610, A611 and A6514, and Carlton is 4.3 km away, Nottingham 5.3 km. The nearest service area is Trent Bridge Services on the A6011, 6.7 km out. In the 2021 Census, 48.5% of working residents in the Arnold built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales 45.1%, and 20.7% of households had no car. In 2025 MOT tests across NG postcodes, the BMW 3 Series was among the five most tested diesel cars. A remapped diesel 3 Series pulls harder through the middle of the revs.

name: Ashford
intro: Diesel still makes up 30.7% of privately kept cars in the Ashford council area, a larger share than the 29.1% across England at the end of June 2026, even after a 6% fall in the number of diesel cars over the year. In the 2021 Census, taken during a lockdown, 8% of working residents in the Ashford built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales. The M20 is on the town's road list, and on a diesel covering that kind of distance, Stage 1 remapping, a change made only to the engine's software and kept within its limits, lifts mid-range torque for overtaking and holding motorway speed.
driving: The closest listed stop is Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070, at 2.9 km, with Stop24 Folkestone Services 12.9 km away on the M20. The A28 and A20 are also on Ashford's road list. Even Hythe, the nearest listed town, is 16 km away, and Canterbury and Sittingbourne are 20.9 km and 24.7 km. In the 2021 Census, 51.3% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales. In 2025 MOT tests across TN postcodes, the Land Rover Discovery was the most tested diesel car, just ahead of the Volkswagen Golf. Whichever you drive, your insurer must be told once a remap is done.

name: Ashington
intro: Ashington's 2021 Census figures pull in two directions. In the built-up area, 29.7% of households had no car, above the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, yet 57.4% of working residents drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales. Where a household does run a car, it is often the way to work, and a car used like that is the one worth looking at for Stage 1 remapping. The remap is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the difference shows in the mid-range: the car pulls from lower revs, overtakes with less effort and needs fewer downshifts.
driving: Local roads include the A189, A196 and A197, with Bedlington 5.4 km away, Morpeth 8.6 km and Cramlington 10.2 km. Seaton Burn Services is 13.3 km out on the A19. In the 2021 Census, only 4% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, a little under the 4.4% for England and Wales. The Northumberland council area had 93 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 for England, and 95.7% of those vans ran on diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NE postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van. A loaded Transit is where Stage 1 earns its keep, though gearbox and clutch limits decide how far a van remap should go.

name: Ashton-in-Makerfield
intro: Ashton-in-Makerfield recorded two or more cars or vans in 41% of households in its built-up area in the 2021 Census, above both the Wigan council area (36.3%) and England and Wales (35.4%). Only 16.6% had no car or van. Where a household runs two vehicles, one of them often does the heavier work. If that one is a diesel covering long runs or pulling a trailer, Stage 1 remapping mainly changes how the engine pulls: more mid-range torque, so overtaking and joining faster roads take less effort and hills need fewer downshifts. Nothing physical is changed: the fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, inside the engine's limits.
driving: The M6 and M58 are both on Ashton's road list, with the A580, A49, A58 and A577, and Burtonwood Services on the M62 is the nearest service area at 8.4 km. Haydock is 3.3 km away, Newton-le-Willows 4.5 km and Golborne 4.6 km. Driving was the usual way to work in the 2021 Census: 59.1% of working residents in the built-up area drove, against 45.1% across England and Wales, even with census day in a lockdown. Across the Wigan council area, privately kept diesel cars fell from 52,463 to 49,121 in the year to June 2026. For those still running one on motorway and A580 journeys, extra mid-range torque is the useful part of a remap. A car with a DPF or EGR fault is repaired before it is remapped.

name: Ashton-under-Lyne
intro: Homes without a car are more common in Ashton-under-Lyne than across Tameside as a whole. In the 2021 Census, 33.8% of households in the Ashton-under-Lyne built-up area had no car, against 26.1% for the Tameside council area and 23.3% across England and Wales, and 24.1% had two or more. When a household relies on one car, keeping it reliable comes first, which is why a vehicle with a DPF, EGR, AdBlue or injector fault is repaired before any Stage 1 remapping is done. On a healthy diesel, the remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and it brings stronger mid-range torque for pulling away and overtaking.
driving: Dukinfield, 2.4 km away, is the nearest neighbour to Ashton-under-Lyne, with Audenshaw and Stalybridge both at 3.5 km. The M60 and M67 are on the road list, along with the A6043, A627 and A635. Just under half of working residents in the built-up area, 49%, drove to work in the 2021 Census, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Across the Tameside council area, only 4% of privately kept cars were plug-ins at the end of June 2026, against 5.3% across England. In 2025 MOT tests across OL postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars. For a Golf or Qashqai, a remap shows up as a car that overtakes with less fuss.

name: Atherton
intro: Tyldesley is just 2.6 km from Atherton, with Westhoughton at 3 km, Leigh at 4.2 km and Little Hulton at 4.6 km. Hops that short rarely ask much of an engine, so the case for Stage 1 remapping here rests on the heavier jobs: a car loaded for a trip away, a van full of tools or a trailer on the back. Extra mid-range torque is what helps there, with fewer downshifts and easier overtaking. The remap changes only the engine's software, its fuel, boost and timing settings, and stays within the limits the engine was built for. Your insurer must be told about it, and any fault with the DPF, EGR or injectors is put right first.
driving: The M61 is the motorway on Atherton's road list, and Rivington Services on it is 9.9 km away. The A579, A577, A6, A58, A580 and A673 cover the rest. In the 2021 Census, 23.9% of households in the built-up area had no car or van, more than the 21.3% across the Wigan council area, and 33% had two or more. Only 2.3% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work. The council area had 12,246 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 96.7% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across M postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter were the most tested diesel vans. A Sprinter or Transit carrying a full load is where a remap's extra torque shows most.

name: Aylesbury

Stage 1 remapping lifts a diesel's torque in the middle of the rev range, by changing the fuel, boost and timing settings in software within the engine's limits, so overtaking and joining faster roads on those runs take less effort. driving: The A41, A413, A418 and A4010 are among Aylesbury's main roads, and Thame Services on the A418 is the nearest listed service area, 13.4 km away, with Bourne End Services on the A41 at 20.5 km. In the 2021 Census, 23.4% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% for England and Wales. Plug-in cars were 6.9% of privately kept cars in the Buckinghamshire council area at the end of June 2026, above the 5.3% for England. In 2025 MOT tests across HP postcodes, the Ford Transit Connect made the top five diesel vans. On a Connect carrying tools, the extra low-rev torque is what you notice most.

name: Ayr
intro: Every service area listed near Ayr is on the M74 and more than 50 km away: the M74 Truck Stop at 50.4 km, RoadChef Hamilton at 51.9 km and Cairn Lodge at 52 km. None of the town's own main roads, the A77, A70, A713, A79 and A719, is a motorway. On long A-road runs like these, Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is mainly about the mid-range. driving: Half of working residents in the Ayr locality, 50.4%, drove to work in Scotland's 2022 Census, against 45.9% across Scotland, and 6.7% travelled 30 km or more, above the Scottish 4.9%. Of the listed neighbours, only Prestwick, at 4.1 km, is under 10 km away, and Kilwinning is 22.7 km off. In the South Ayrshire council area, 28.3% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, slightly above the 27.7% for Scotland. Among diesels given an MOT in KA postcodes in 2025, the Ford Focus was the most tested car and the Ford Transit the most tested van. With a Transit loaded for work, gearbox and clutch limits matter, and the gain shows as firmer pulling under load.

name: Bamber Bridge
intro: Driving was how most working residents of Bamber Bridge got to work in the 2021 Census. A car that does the commute every day is the one where Stage 1 remapping is felt most often, because the gain shows up on every journey rather than only on long trips. If you run a van for work, that is often where extra low-rev torque shows most, as long as the clutch and gearbox can take it.

name: Barking and Dagenham
intro: None of the 104 largest towns we cover held on to its diesel cars better than Barking and Dagenham. Privately kept diesel cars in the council area went from 12,085 to 11,907 in the year to the end of June 2026, a fall of only 1.5%. Diesel still makes up about 19% of the 61,484 private cars there. Diesels are leaving the road slowly here, and for owners who plan to keep one, Stage 1 remapping is a way to get more from it. It is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel, the gain most people notice is mid-range torque: easier overtaking and smoother joins onto fast roads.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 32.5% of working residents in the Barking and Dagenham council area drove to work, well below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 25.6% travelled 10 km or more, above the England and Wales figure of 19%. The nearest service area is Moto Thurrock on the M25, about 11 km away. The council area also has 2,967 privately kept vans, 95.1% of them diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across RM postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van. For a loaded Transit, a remap's extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits. The London ULEZ covers every borough and can charge cars and vans. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether you pay.

name: Barnet
intro: Barnet sits 7th of the 104 largest towns we cover for plug-in cars, which make up 9% of the 130,542 privately kept cars in the council area. Diesel, at 12.4%, is one of the lowest shares in the same group. Both figures are for the end of June 2026. If yours is one of the diesels still on Barnet's roads, a Stage 1 remap changes how it drives, not what it runs on. The engine's settings are adjusted in software, inside its limits, and the extra mid-range torque shows when you overtake or join a fast road. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive, so treat it as a side effect, not the reason.
driving: The M1, A1, A41 and A406 are among Barnet's main roads. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 4.4 km away and South Mimms on the A1(M) is 8.2 km, so a run out of London starts close by. In the 2021 Census, 25.1% of working residents in the Barnet council area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 29.9% of households had no car. In 2025 MOT tests across NW postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. The ULEZ covers every London borough, and its daily charge can apply to cars and vans. A remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it does not change whether that charge applies.

name: Barnsley
intro: The M1 and the A628 could hardly be more different, yet both are on Barnsley's list of main roads. One is a motorway, with Moto Woolley Edge services 8.7 km from the town in a straight line; the other heads west across the Peak District towards Manchester. A diesel that covers both kinds of driving, motorway miles one week and a long cross-country run the next, is a good fit for Stage 1 remapping. It is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside the engine's limits, with no parts added. The gain most drivers notice is mid-range torque, so hills need fewer downshifts and joining the motorway from a slip road takes less effort.
driving: Royston and Cudworth and Shafton are each 4.5 km away in a straight line, Darton 4.6 km and Wombwell 5.8 km, and the A61, A635 and A633 are also main roads. In the 2021 Census, 28.4% of households in the Barnsley built-up area had no car, more than the 22.7% across the Barnsley council area, yet 56.3% of working residents drove to work. Diesel is strong in the council area: at the end of June 2026, 38.3% of privately kept cars there ran on it, against 29.1% across England, and so did 96.6% of private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across S postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van. As with any diesel, a Transit is only remapped once any DPF or EGR fault is fixed.

name: Barrow-in-Furness
intro: Only 9.9% of working residents in the Barrow-in-Furness built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, against 19% across England and Wales. Census day fell in a lockdown, so commuting ran low everywhere, but the gap suggests most work trips from Barrow stayed close to home. For Stage 1 remapping, that changes what matters. On short urban runs the useful gain is pull from low revs, so the car moves off cleanly and holds a higher gear without labouring. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on, and a diesel with a DPF fault is repaired before any of it starts.
driving: Barrow has water on three sides: Morecambe Bay, the Duddon Estuary and the Irish Sea. Its main roads are the A590, A595 and A5087, Ulverston is 12.1 km away, and the nearest motorway stop, Burton-in-Kendal Services on the M6, is 32.7 km out. In the 2021 Census, 29.1% of households in the built-up area had no car or van, above the Barrow-in-Furness council area (26.9%) and England and Wales (23.3%). Across the Westmorland and Furness council area, 35.5% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% for England. In 2025 MOT tests across LA postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars and the Ford Transit the vans. Out on the A590, extra mid-range torque makes overtaking slower traffic easier.

name: Barry
intro: Of the places nearest to Barry, only Penarth and Cardiff are close by, at 6.7 km and 11.4 km. After them the gap widens, with Church Village 17.7 km away and Caerphilly 19 km. Reaching those towns means a sustained drive rather than a quick hop, and steady driving like that is where a diesel with Stage 1 remapping feels stronger. Joining faster traffic and overtaking both rely on mid-range torque, which is what the remap adds. Fuel, boost and timing are adjusted in software inside the engine's limits, with no extra parts, and the car pulls more willingly in a higher gear.
driving: Barry's main roads are four A roads, the A4055, A4050, A4226 and A4231, and the nearest motorway stop is Cardiff West Services on the M4, 11.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 53.7% of working residents of the Barry built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, but only 2.7% travelled 30 km or more, against 4.4%. Diesel was 30.6% of privately kept cars in the Vale of Glamorgan council area at the end of June 2026, well below the Wales figure of 36.1%. In 2025 MOT tests across CF postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus were the two most tested diesel cars. On either car, Stage 1 is felt most when overtaking on the A roads out of town.

name: Basildon
intro: Long journeys to work stand out in the Basildon figures. In the 2021 Census, 7.4% of working residents in the Basildon built-up area travelled 30 km or more in a straight line, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and 21.8% travelled at least 10 km. Those figures come from a lockdown census day, so commuting was lower than usual. For a diesel that covers that kind of distance, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about how the engine pulls at speed: more mid-range torque for overtaking and joining fast roads, and less need to change down. Nothing is bolted on. The remap adjusts fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits.
driving: The main part of Basildon sits between two dual carriageways, the A127 to the north and the A13 to the south, and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 7.3 km away. In the 2021 Census, 48.7% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. At the end of June 2026 the Basildon council area had 89,209 privately kept cars, 24.3% diesel and 62.2% petrol, and 6,739 private vans, 94% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across SS postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. On a loaded van, Stage 1 adds mid-range pull, within what the clutch and gearbox can handle.

name: Basingstoke
intro: Two-car households are common in Basingstoke. In the 2021 Census, 40.9% of households in the Basingstoke built-up area had two or more cars, well above the England and Wales figure of 35.4%, and only 17.8% had none, against 23.3%. More cars per home means more choice over which one does the long runs, carries the load or tows, and that is usually the one worth looking at for Stage 1 remapping. The work is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, within its limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the gain you feel is mid-range torque, so the car pulls cleanly from low revs and needs fewer downshifts.
driving: The M3 is among Basingstoke's main roads, with the A339, A33 and A30, and the closest service area is Popham on the A303, 11.9 km away. In the 2021 Census, 5.2% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales. In the Basingstoke and Deane council area, 28.3% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, and their number fell 7% over the year, one of the steepest falls of the 104 largest towns we cover. In 2025 MOT tests across RG postcodes, the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz E Class were among the most tested diesel cars. On cars like these, a remap mainly means easier overtaking and smoother joins onto the M3.

name: Bath

caz.name: Bath Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers central Bath and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: Central Bath is covered by the Bath Clean Air Zone, a Class C charging zone that applies to vans but does not charge private cars. A Stage 1 remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it makes no difference either way to whether the zone charges your van. What it does change is how the engine delivers its pulling power. Fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits, and on a diesel the gain is mid-range torque. For a van carrying tools or materials around the city, that means stronger pulling when loaded and fewer gear changes, while the gearbox and clutch set how far the remap should go.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 28.5% of households in the Bath built-up area had no car, more than the England and Wales figure of 23.3% and the 19.9% across the Bath and North East Somerset council area. Only 27.7% of working residents drove to work. Moto Leigh Delamere on the M4, 20.3 km away, is the nearest listed service area, and the main roads are A roads such as the A4, A36, A46 and A367. Keynsham is 9.7 km from the city and Trowbridge 13.2 km. Just 26.8% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars, against 35.4% in England and Wales. Where a household does run a diesel, a remap's extra mid-range torque helps when joining the A36 or A46 out of the city, getting up to speed with fewer downshifts.

name: Batley
intro: Heckmondwike, Dewsbury and Morley all lie within 4 km of Batley in a straight line, at 2.3 km, 3.8 km and 3.9 km, with Liversedge at 4.3 km. Towns this close together mean a lot of driving happens in short stages at lower revs, which is the range Stage 1 remapping improves most. The remap is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside the engine's limits, with no parts added. A diesel gains torque in the middle of the rev range, so it pulls away from junctions more cleanly and holds a higher gear without labouring. How fuel use changes depends on how the vehicle is driven, and any difference is modest.
driving: For longer runs, the M62, M621 and M1 are all among Batley's main roads, and Welcome Break Hartshead Moor services on the M62 is 7 km away, with Moto Woolley Edge on the M1 at 12.4 km. Its A roads include the A62, A638 and A653. In the 2021 Census, 55.4% of working residents in the Batley built-up area drove to work, slightly above the Kirklees council area's 53.1%, and 32.8% of households had two or more cars. In 2025 MOT tests across WF postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, followed by the Volkswagen Transporter and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. For a loaded van joining the M62, the extra torque from a remap is the part you feel, within the limits of the gearbox and clutch.

name: Bearsden
intro: Most households in the Bearsden locality ran at least one car in Scotland's 2022 Census, and 46.4% had two or more. Only 10.1% had no car, far below the Scotland figure of 26.4%. With two cars on many drives, Stage 1 remapping is something to weigh up one vehicle at a time. It is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel, the most noticeable change is mid-range torque, which makes joining faster roads and overtaking feel less strained. Your insurer must be told about a remap, so allow for that on each car you change.
driving: Milngavie lies 2.6 km from Bearsden and Clydebank 4.8 km, while the road list runs to eight A roads, the A81, A82, A739 and A809 among them. The closest service area is RoadChef Bothwell Services on the M74, 20.6 km off. In the 2022 Census, 14.9% of working residents travelled 10 km or more, under the Scotland figure of 20.4%. Diesel was 21.5% of privately kept cars in the East Dunbartonshire council area at the end of June 2026, below the 27.7% for Scotland, and private diesel cars there fell 12.7% over the year. With only 52 private vans per 1,000 private cars, a remap enquiry here is more likely to be for a car than a van.

name: Bebington
intro: The car was the commonest way to work in Bebington in the 2021 Census: 53.4% of working residents in the built-up area drove, more than the 51.3% across the Wirral council area and the 45.1% across England and Wales. That was on a census day in lockdown. A car used for a daily commute is where Stage 1 remapping is felt every day rather than once in a while. On a diesel, the extra mid-range torque makes joining faster roads and overtaking easier, and you change down less often. No parts are added: the fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software and kept inside the engine's limits.
driving: Bebington lies on the eastern side of the Wirral Peninsula, with the M53 and A41 at the top of its road list. Birkenhead is 6.2 km away, Neston 6.4 km, Ellesmere Port 9.2 km and Liverpool 9.3 km. The nearest service area, Earlsfield on the M57, is 15.1 km away. In the 2021 Census, 38.2% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars or vans, against 32.5% across the Wirral council area. Diesel made up 28.4% of the council area's privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, slightly below England's 29.1%. In 2025 MOT tests across CH postcodes, the Ford Transit and Vauxhall Vivaro led the diesel vans. For a van that works loaded, the gearbox and clutch set how far a remap should go.

name: Bedford
intro: Households in Bedford itself are less likely to have a car than those in the surrounding council area. In the 2021 Census, 24.8% of households in the Bedford built-up area had no car, against 18.2% across the Bedford council area and 23.3% across England and Wales, and 32.7% had two or more. For a household where one car does every job, from short trips across town to runs along the A421, Stage 1 remapping is a way to make that car more flexible. It adjusts the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within its limits. On a diesel the gain is mid-range torque: stronger pull from low revs and fewer downshifts. Your insurer must be told about the change.
driving: Bedford Services on the A421 is 3.9 km from the town, and Crawley Crossing Truck Stop on the M1 is 16.3 km away. Kempston is only 3.6 km off. In the 2021 Census, 5.4% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. Vans are less common in the Bedford council area than across England, at 63 per 1,000 private cars against 81 at the end of June 2026. The Mercedes-Benz C Class and E Class were both among the five most tested diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across MK postcodes. In a C Class or E Class, a remap shows as easier overtaking on the A421 and A6.

name: Bedworth
intro: From Bedworth to Corley Services on the M6 is just 4 km in a straight line, and the M69 is also among the main roads around the town. With two motorways that close, plenty of journeys from CV12 include a motorway stretch, and motorway driving shows off what Stage 1 remapping does well. The remap is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the difference is mid-range torque: steadier progress past slower lorries and less need to drop a gear when traffic speeds up again. If the car already has a fault, such as a DPF or EGR problem, that is repaired first.
driving: Nuneaton and Coventry are both within 7.3 km of Bedworth, with Hinckley at 10.7 km, and the A444 and A4254 are among the local roads. In the 2021 Census, 58.8% of working residents in the Bedworth built-up area drove to work, well above the 45.1% across England and Wales, yet only 3.5% travelled 30 km or more. That points to plenty of short car journeys, even allowing for census day falling in a lockdown. Diesel is common in the wider borough: in the Nuneaton and Bedworth council area, 33.8% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% across England. For short, regular runs, the Stage 1 that suits helps a diesel pull cleanly from low revs rather than chasing top speed.

name: Beeston
intro: Fewer than four in ten working residents of the Beeston built-up area drove to work in the 2021 Census: 38.5%, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1% and the Broxtowe council area's 46.9%. Census day fell in a lockdown, so treat that as a snapshot of an unusual time rather than a measure of today. Even so, it suggests the car was not always the default way to get to work here. For those who do drive, Stage 1 remapping alters three things in the engine software, fuel, boost and timing, without going past the engine's limits or adding any parts. On a diesel the benefit is extra torque in the middle of the rev range, which makes merging and overtaking easier.
driving: Neighbouring places sit close around Beeston: Stapleford is 2.5 km away, Clifton 4.2 km, Long Eaton 5 km and Nottingham 6.1 km. The M1, A52 and A453 are among the main roads, and Trowell Services on the M1 is 4.8 km out. Most journeys to work were short in the 2021 Census, with only 13% of working residents in the built-up area travelling 10 km or more. Across the Broxtowe council area, diesel was 28.9% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, slightly below England's 29.1%, and the number of private diesel cars fell 6.2% over the year, faster than the 5.3% fall in England. If you are keeping a diesel for the A52 and M1, a remap makes those runs feel less laboured.

name: Belfast

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021 (Scotland: 20 March 2022). England and Wales census day fell in a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual.

intro: Belfast drivers have been slow to plug in. Only 2.7% of privately kept cars in the council area were plug-ins at the end of June 2026, the lowest share of the 104 largest towns we cover. Diesel goes the other way: at 36.9%, Belfast has the 3rd highest diesel share of the 104, which comes to 45,030 private diesel cars. Where diesel is still the everyday car, Stage 1 remapping is a practical way to make one more pleasant to drive. Fuel, boost and timing are adjusted in the engine software, the changes stay inside the engine's limits, and no parts are added. What you feel is mid-range pull: overtaking with less effort and fewer downshifts when the road climbs.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 47.2% of working residents in the Belfast council area drove to work, but only 8.8% travelled 10 km or more, and a third of households, 33.9%, had no car. Lisburn Services on the M1 is about 9 km away, and Applegreen Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 about 12 km. The diesel count is falling slowly, down 2.8% over the year to June 2026, one of the smallest falls of the 104. The council area also has 5,847 privately kept vans, 97.5% of them diesel. A van that works loaded gains useful torque from a remap, though its gearbox and clutch still set the limits. If an AdBlue, DPF or EGR fault is showing, that is repaired before any remap.

name: Beverley
intro: Beverley's working residents often had a long trip to work in the 2021 Census: 29.1% of those in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more, against 19% across England and Wales, and 6.7% went 30 km or more. For drivers covering that kind of distance, what matters is how the engine pulls once it is up to speed, and that is the part Stage 1 remapping changes. It alters the fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the limits the engine was built for, and adds no hardware. On a diesel, stronger torque in the middle of the rev range means fewer downshifts and easier overtaking. Any change in fuel use is modest and depends on how the car is driven.
driving: Beverley's main roads are the A1035, A164, A1079 and A1174, and the nearest service area is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, 26.3 km away. Cottingham is 6.5 km off in a straight line and Kingston upon Hull 10.7 km. Only 18.7% of households in the built-up area had no car in the 2021 Census, below the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. Across the East Riding of Yorkshire council area there were 95 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, compared with 81 in England. In 2025 MOT tests across HU postcodes, the Nissan Qashqai was the most tested diesel car. On a car like that, a remap brings smoother, stronger acceleration in the gears you use most.

name: Bexhill-on-Sea
intro: In the Rother council area, which takes in Bexhill-on-Sea, there were 117 privately kept vans for every 1,000 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, well above the England figure of 81. Of Rother's 6,190 private vans, 92% ran on diesel. That makes Stage 1 remapping as much a van question here as a car one. The change is made in software, to the fuel, boost and timing settings, and stays within the engine's limits. On a loaded van or one pulling a trailer, what you feel is stronger torque low in the rev range, so it holds a gear on a hill instead of dropping down. Gearbox and clutch limits matter on a van, and they decide how far the remap should go.
driving: Driving out of Bexhill-on-Sea means A roads: the A259, A269, A271, A2036, A2690 and A2691, with no motorway on the list. Hastings is 8.7 km away and Eastbourne 13.1 km. The closest service area, Polegate Services on the A22, is 15 km off. In the 2021 Census, taken during a lockdown, 51.3% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, above the 45.1% for England and Wales. Diesel made up 26.7% of privately kept cars in the Rother council area at the end of June 2026, below England's 29.1%. At TN postcode MOT stations in 2025, the Land Rover Discovery was the most tested diesel car, and on a Discovery with a trailer behind it, Stage 1 means fewer downshifts on the A259.

name: Bexley
intro: Seven in ten privately kept cars in the Bexley council area run on petrol: 70.8% of 98,067 at the end of June 2026. Diesel makes up 13.5%, one of the lowest shares among the 104 largest towns we cover, and private diesel cars fell from 14,230 to 13,259 over the year, one of the steepest drops in that group. So a Stage 1 remap here is often a petrol question as well as a diesel one. The principle is the same on both: software settings for fuel, boost and timing are changed within the engine's limits, and no parts are added. On the diesels that remain, the gain you notice most is mid-range pull.
driving: The A2 and A13 are among Bexley's main roads, and the nearest listed service area is Moto Thurrock on the M25, 9 km away, with Tollgate on the A2 at 15.9 km. In the 2021 Census, 36% of working residents in the Bexley council area drove to work and 32.3% of households had two or more cars. The council area has 4,772 privately kept vans, 90.9% of them diesel, and the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van in 2025 MOT tests across DA postcodes. On a loaded van, extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits. Bexley is inside the ULEZ, where a daily charge can apply to cars and vans, and a remap leaves the emissions standard as it was, so it does not change that.

name: Bicester
intro: Moto Cherwell Valley Services on the M40 is just 6.4 km from Bicester, and Welcome Break Oxford Services, on the same motorway, is 18.3 km away. If your journeys often take you onto the M40, Stage 1 remapping is worth understanding. No parts are added. The remap changes the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software, staying inside the limits the engine was designed for. On a diesel, the difference shows up as mid-range torque: getting up to speed from a slip road takes less effort, and a gap in traffic is easier to use. Any change in fuel use is modest and depends on how you drive. A vehicle with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired before it is remapped.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 27.6% of working residents in the Bicester built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, above both the 19% for England and Wales and the 23.3% for the Cherwell council area. Only 14.2% of households had no car. The town sits where two Roman roads crossed, and its road list runs to the A41, A34, A4421 and A4095 as well as the M40. Kidlington is 12.6 km away, Brackley 14.8 km and Oxford 17.4 km, and Peartree Services on the A44 is 14.6 km out. Among diesel vans given an MOT across OX postcodes in 2025, the Volkswagen Transporter came close behind the Ford Transit. For a Transporter carrying tools, extra low-down pull is the useful part, within its gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Billericay
intro: In the 2021 Census, 38.3% of working residents in the Billericay built-up area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. That was not for lack of cars: only 11.5% of households had none, against 23.3% across England and Wales, and 46.1% had two or more. Census day also fell in a lockdown, so the commuting share is a snapshot of an unusual day. Whatever a Billericay car is used for, Stage 1 remapping works the same way: the fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. On a diesel you feel it as mid-range torque, so the car pulls from low revs without hunting for a lower gear.
driving: Billericay's main roads include the A127 and A12. Basildon is 6.5 km away and Brentwood 8.6 km. For a break on a longer run, Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 13.2 km off and Moto Thurrock on the M25 18.5 km. In the 2021 Census, 7.2% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales. Diesel was 24.3% of privately kept cars in the Basildon council area at the end of June 2026, below the 29.1% across England. In 2025 MOT tests across CM postcodes, the Ford Kuga and Land Rover Discovery were the two most tested diesel cars. With a trailer behind a Kuga or Discovery, extra pull on the A127 is the gain you notice.

name: Billingham
intro: Within 7 km of Billingham there are three service areas: Wolviston Services on the A689 at 4 km, the southbound Ron Perry A19 services at 6.6 km and Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 at 6.7 km. They follow the main roads in and around the town, the A19, A66 and A689 among them. Those are roads where Stage 1 remapping shows, because pulling power at speed is what it improves. The remap changes the fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. On a diesel, stronger mid-range torque makes joining the A19 and overtaking on the A66 easier, with fewer downshifts along the way.
driving: Stockton-on-Tees is 4.6 km from Billingham, Thornaby-on-Tees 5.3 km and Middlesbrough 6.6 km, and the postcode districts include TS23 and TS20. In the 2021 Census, 33.6% of households in the Billingham built-up area had two or more cars, a little below the England and Wales figure of 35.4%, while 60.2% of working residents drove to work. The Stockton-on-Tees council area had 33.3% diesel among its privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, above England's 29.1%. Of the diesel vans given an MOT in TS postcodes in 2025, the Peugeot Partner was among the five most tested. A small van carrying tools or stock pulls better from low revs after a remap, and the insurer needs to be told.

name: Bilston
intro: Five neighbouring places lie within 4 km of Bilston: Darlaston is the nearest at 2.8 km, followed by Tipton, Coseley, Willenhall and Wednesbury. That makes much local driving short and urban, which is worth bearing in mind with Stage 1 remapping. Nothing is fitted to the car: the change is to the fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine software, kept inside the engine's limits. What it gives a diesel is mid-range torque, so the car moves off more willingly and holds a gear for longer between junctions. Before any remap, a vehicle with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first, and that matters on a diesel that rarely gets a long run.
driving: In the Bilston built-up area, 56% of working residents drove to work in the 2021 Census, compared with 45.1% across England and Wales. Fewer households had two or more cars, though: 26.8%, against 35.4%. For motorway trips the M6 is on the road list, with Moto Hilton Park Services 9 km away, while the A41, A463 and A4123 serve local journeys. In the Wolverhampton council area, 35.3% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, above England's 29.1%, and 97% of private vans were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across WV postcodes, the Nissan Qashqai was the third most tested diesel car. What a Qashqai on the A41 gains from Stage 1 is smoother pull from low revs, not extra speed.

name: Birkenhead
intro: A third of households in the Birkenhead built-up area had no car in the 2021 Census: 33.1%, against 23.3% for England and Wales. Yet 51% of working residents drove to work, so the cars that are owned on this side of the Mersey tend to be used every day. That was a lockdown census day, so read it as a snapshot. For a diesel in daily use, Stage 1 remapping changes the mid-range, which is where it pulls out of junctions, climbs and joins faster roads. A remap is no cure for a fault, though: any DPF or EGR problem is repaired first.
driving: The M53 is the only motorway on Birkenhead's main road list, with the A41, A552 and A554 among the A roads, and Wallasey is 3.6 km away. The closest listed service area, Earlsfield Services on the M57, is 16.1 km off. Across the Wirral council area there were 149,775 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 28.4% of them diesel, and private diesel cars fell from 45,221 to 42,551 over the year. Private vans numbered 10,454, and 95.5% were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across CH postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. Loaded vans feel Stage 1 torque most, and an insurer must be told about any remap.

name: Birmingham

caz.name: Birmingham Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers the city centre inside the A4540 Middleway and applies to cars and vans.

intro: Birmingham's Clean Air Zone is a Class D charging zone covering the city centre inside the A4540 Middleway ring road, though not the Middleway itself, and it applies to both cars and vans. Inside the zone or out of it, Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is felt as mid-range torque: joining the M6 or the A38(M) from a slip road and overtaking on the A45 become noticeably easier. The change is to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits. It does not alter the emissions standard, so a car or van the zone charges today is charged after a remap too, and one it does not charge stays that way.
driving: At the end of June 2026 the Birmingham council area had 411,153 privately kept cars. Only 3.6% were plug-ins, one of the lowest shares of the 104 largest towns we cover, and 27.1% were diesel, about 111,000 cars. In the 2021 Census, 32.9% of households in the Birmingham built-up area had no car, above the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, yet 46.2% of working residents drove to work. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter were the most tested diesel vans, with the Volkswagen Golf and BMW 3 Series top among cars. A loaded Sprinter or Transit gains stronger pull at low revs from Stage 1, though the gearbox and clutch limits still set how far a van's remap should go.

name: Bishop's Stortford
intro: Just 2.3 km separates Bishop's Stortford from Welcome Break Birchanger Green Services on the M11, so the motorway starts almost on the doorstep. Longer commutes were also more common than average: in the 2021 Census, 7.6% of working residents in the Bishop's Stortford built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and that was on a census day in lockdown. For drivers who spend time on the M11, Stage 1 remapping changes the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within its limits. On a diesel the gain is torque in the middle of the rev range, so pulling out to pass a lorry or merging from a slip road needs fewer downshifts.
driving: Stansted Airport lies just east of the M11, and four A-roads complete the town's list: the A120, A1250, A1060 and A1184. Sawbridgeworth is the nearest neighbour at 6.6 km, with Harlow at 11.7 km. In the 2021 Census, 38.3% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, under the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 42.2% of households had two or more cars. In the East Hertfordshire council area, diesel made up 22.2% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% across England. The Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car in 2025 MOT tests across CM postcodes. Loaded for a long trip or hitched to a trailer, a Kuga feels a remap mostly as easier pull at low revs.

name: Blackburn
intro: Blackburn with Darwen has the 2nd highest share of diesel cars of the 104 largest towns we cover. At the end of June 2026, 38.5% of the council area's 64,075 privately kept cars ran on diesel, and their number had fallen by only 2.1% in a year, one of the smallest drops of the 104. With that many diesels in daily use, the order of work matters. A diesel with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first, and Stage 1 remapping comes after, once the engine is healthy. The remap then lifts mid-range torque, which is where a diesel does its everyday work: overtaking, hills and joining faster roads.
driving: ExtraMSA Blackburn with Darwen Services, on the M65, is under 4 km from the town, and the A666, A677 and A59 are among its main roads. In the 2021 Census, 55.6% of working residents in the Blackburn built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. The council area has 4,039 privately kept vans, 96.6% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BB postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car by a wide margin, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, with the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter and Volkswagen Transporter behind. A remap gives a Golf easier pace on the M65 and a loaded van more torque, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Blackpool
intro: Blackpool keeps more vans per car than most of the towns we cover: 90 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars in the council area, the 7th highest ratio of the 104 largest towns we cover. That came to 5,007 vans at the end of June 2026, and 96.1% of them run on diesel. For a van, a Stage 1 remap is mostly about torque. With more pull from low revs, a loaded van or one towing a trailer holds its gear longer and needs fewer downshifts. Gearbox and clutch limits still matter, so the remap file has to be matched to the vehicle rather than chosen for the biggest possible gain.
driving: The M55 is the only motorway on Blackpool's list of main roads, alongside A-roads such as the A583 and A584, and the nearest listed service area, Lancaster on the M6, is 24.9 km away. Commutes were short in the 2021 Census: only 10.4% of working residents in the Blackpool built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales, although 49.9% drove. Lytham St Anne's is 5.3 km away and Poulton-le-Fylde 6.4 km. Of the 55,696 private cars in the council area, 32.1% are diesel and only 3.2% plug-in, one of the lowest plug-in shares of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across FY postcodes, the BMW 3 Series was the most tested diesel car. Any DPF or other fault is repaired before a remap.

name: Bletchley
intro: The M1 carries all three of the service areas closest to Bletchley: Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 9.7 km, Newport Pagnell Services at 10 km and Toddington Services at 16.9 km. The motorway is not on the town's own road list, which is made up of the A421, A5, A4146 and A509, so a motorway trip from here starts with an A-road run. Stage 1 remapping helps on both parts of that journey. The software change to fuel, boost and timing stays within the engine's limits, nothing is bolted on, and on a diesel it lifts mid-range torque, so the car gets away from junctions more cleanly and settles at motorway speed sooner.
driving: Milton Keynes is 5.2 km away and Leighton Buzzard 9.5 km, with Buckingham at 17 km. In the 2021 Census, 49.6% of working residents in the Bletchley built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% for England and Wales and 43.7% for the Milton Keynes council area. Only 13.2% travelled 10 km or more, below the 19% for England and Wales, yet 5.3% went 30 km or more, against 4.4%, so short local commutes sat alongside a share of long ones. In 2025 MOT tests across MK postcodes, the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz C Class were among the most tested diesel cars. In a saloon like these, a remap is mostly felt on the longer runs, as easier overtaking and less gear changing.

name: Bloxwich
intro: Moto Hilton Park on the M6 is 5.3 km from Bloxwich in a straight line, and RoadChef Norton Canes on the M6 Toll is 6.3 km. The M54 and M5 are on the town's road list as well, so a diesel here can spend part of the week in local traffic and part of it at motorway speed. Stage 1 remapping suits that split. The work is done in software, with the engine's fuel, boost and timing adjusted and held within its limits, and no parts are added. On a diesel the gain sits in the mid-range, where you need it for a motorway merge or a quick overtake. Fuel use may change a little either way, depending on how the vehicle is driven.
driving: Pelsall is 2.8 km away, Rushall and Shelfield 3 km and Walsall 4 km, so many local trips are short. In the 2021 Census, 30.9% of households in the Bloxwich built-up area had no car, above the 25% for the Walsall council area, yet 58.2% of working residents drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales. The A34 and A4148 are among the main roads for those journeys. In 2025 MOT tests across WS postcodes, the Ford Focus was the second most tested diesel car, just behind the Volkswagen Golf. Stage 1 on a Focus that mixes short runs with the odd motorway trip sharpens low-rev response, and any DPF fault is repaired before the remap goes on.

name: Blyth
intro: Ten kilometres or more: that was the journey to work for 27.5% of working residents in the Blyth built-up area at the 2021 Census, against 19% across England and Wales. And 56.8% drove to work, compared with 45.1%. Regular runs out of town like these are a good reason to look at Stage 1 remapping. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, inside the engine's limits, and on a diesel the gain is mid-range torque, so joining the A189 and overtaking slower traffic take less effort. Any change to fuel economy is modest and depends on how you drive, so it is the pulling power, not the running cost, that most people notice.
driving: Blyth's road list runs to eight A-roads, from the A193 and A1061 to the A1147 and A1171, and no motorway. Bedlington is 4.7 km away and Whitley Bay 9.1 km, while Seaton Burn Services, on the A19, is 9.2 km out. In the 2021 Census, 30.3% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars, below the 35.4% for England and Wales. Across the Northumberland council area, diesel made up 33.2% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, above England's 29.1%. Among diesel cars given an MOT at test stations in NE postcodes in 2025, the Volkswagen Golf and Nissan Qashqai were the two most tested. On both, a remap shows up as stronger pull from low revs, not a higher top speed.

name: Bognor Regis
intro: Car commuting stood at 56% of working residents in the Bognor Regis built-up area in the 2021 Census, ahead of the Arun council area's 54.6% and the 45.1% across England and Wales. The figure dates from a lockdown, when fewer people were commuting than usual. Across the Arun council area, privately kept vans ran at 96 per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, above England's 81. For a van that carries tools or materials, Stage 1 remapping adds torque in the mid-range, which helps when it is loaded or towing. The remap is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits. On a van, gearbox and clutch limits matter.
driving: The town's road list stops at two A roads, the A259 and A29. Off that list, Fontwell Services is 7.5 km away on the A27, and Farlington Services, on the same road, 25.4 km. Barnham, 5.9 km off, is the nearest listed place, with Chichester at 8.2 km. In the 2021 Census, 4.9% of working residents in the Bognor Regis built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, a little above the 4.4% for England and Wales. In 2025 MOT tests across PO postcodes, the BMW 1 Series and BMW 3 Series were both among the five most tested diesel cars. On a diesel BMW, the remap is felt as stronger pull out of junctions and on the overtake. Your insurer needs to know about it.

name: Bolton
intro: At the end of June 2026, 38,380 privately kept cars in the Bolton council area ran on diesel, 30.1% of the 127,512 total and down from 40,395 a year earlier. That is still a large pool of cars for which Stage 1 remapping is worth a look. Bolton sits in the foothills of the West Pennine Moors, so climbs come with ordinary driving, and the change most diesel owners notice is in the mid-range: fewer downshifts on hills, easier overtaking and a calmer pull with passengers or a trailer. The work is software only, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits.
driving: Rivington Services on the M61 is 9.3 km away, and the A666, A673, A58 and A6 are on the main road list. In the 2021 Census, 52.9% of working residents in the Bolton built-up area drove to work, well above 45.1% for England and Wales, but only 2% travelled 30 km or more, so most commutes were local. Petrol cars made up 53.8% of the council area's privately kept cars and petrol hybrids 11.1%. The 8,184 private vans were 96.6% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BL postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, and the Volkswagen Golf led the cars. On a working van, Stage 1 torque helps with a load, provided the clutch and gearbox are in good order.

name: Bootle
intro: Bootle recorded 41.9% of households without a car in its built-up area at the 2021 Census, well above the England and Wales figure of 23.3% and the Sefton council area's 26.4%. Only 18.1% had two or more cars. In a home with one car, that car covers the commute, the shopping and the longer runs alike, so how it drives day to day matters more than outright pace. Stage 1 remapping is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with no hardware added. On a diesel, the difference most people notice is in the mid-range: the engine pulls more readily from low revs and needs fewer gear changes.
driving: Seven postcode districts cover Bootle, from L4 and L5 up to L30, and the M57 and M58 are both on its road list along with the A565, A5036 and A59. Litherland lies 2 km away, Crosby 4 km and Liverpool 7.1 km. The nearest service area is Old Meadow on the M58, 8.5 km off. Across the Sefton council area, privately kept diesel cars fell by 6.4% in the year to June 2026, a sharper drop than England's 5.3%. In 2025 MOT tests across L postcodes, the Ford Focus and Ford Kuga were the most tested diesel cars. For anyone keeping a diesel like these rather than replacing it, a remap is one way to get more from the engine, and your insurer needs to know about it.

name: Borehamwood
intro: London Gateway Services on the M1 is only 3.1 km from Borehamwood, and South Mimms on the A1(M) is 4.8 km away. The M25, A1 and A41 are on the town's road list as well, so a fast road is never far off, and how a car behaves when it joins one matters. Stage 1 remapping is a software job: the fuel, boost and timing settings are revised, the engine stays within its limits and nothing is bolted on. On a diesel, the extra mid-range torque means merging at motorway speed and overtaking take less planning, and a heavier car feels less laboured when it is loaded.
driving: Long commutes were uncommon from Borehamwood in the 2021 Census: only 2% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, under half the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 40.2% drove to work, against 45.1%. Five places lie within about 9 km, from Bushey at 5.8 km to Watford at 9.1 km, with Barnet and Potters Bar in between. In the Hertsmere council area, just 15.1% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, about half England's 29.1%, and 65.5% were petrol. Across WD postcodes in 2025 MOT tests, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter was the third most tested diesel van. Remapped, a loaded Sprinter pulls away from junctions and up slip roads with less effort.

name: Boston
intro: The diesel car count in Boston council area fell by 2.2% over the year to June 2026, from 16,148 to 15,786, while England as a whole saw a 5.3% fall. Diesel still made up 43.8% of private cars in the council area at that point, against 29.1% across England. Plenty of owners there are evidently keeping their diesels, and for them a remap changes how the engine pulls without any change of car. Stage 1 remapping leaves the hardware alone and works on the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, inside its limits. On a diesel, the reward is extra mid-range pull when overtaking or towing.
driving: Spalding, the closest neighbouring town, is 23.5 km from Boston, with Sleaford at 26.2 km and Skegness at 29.6 km. The A16 and A52 are among the main roads, and Sutterton Services on the A16 is 10.2 km away, with Bicker Bar on the A52 at 10.3 km. Distance shows in the 2021 Census too: 31.6% of working residents in the Boston built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales, and 6.2% went 30 km or more. Among diesel cars, the Land Rover Discovery made the top five in 2025 MOT tests across PE postcodes. For a Discovery pulling a trailer, or any diesel covering long miles on the A16 and A52, Stage 1 is felt as stronger pull when passing slower traffic.

name: Bournemouth
intro: For every 1,000 privately kept cars in the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole council area there are 97 privately kept vans, the second highest ratio of the 104 largest towns we cover. That came to 18,848 private vans at the end of June 2026, and 94.2% of them run on diesel. A van that spends the day loaded, or pulling a trailer, is where Stage 1 remapping makes the clearest difference. Only the software changes: the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits. Extra mid-range torque means easier pulling away and fewer downshifts with weight on board, while the gearbox and clutch decide how far a van's remap should sensibly go.
driving: Commutes around Bournemouth were short in the 2021 Census: only 10.5% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales. Poole is 5.8 km away and Christchurch 9.1 km, and the main roads include the A338, A35, A3049 and A348. The nearest service area, Picket Post on the A31, is 16.2 km out. In 2025 MOT tests across BH postcodes, the Volkswagen Transporter was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Ford Transit, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. Of the council area's 194,180 private cars, 27.5% are diesel. On short runs the useful part of a remap is low-rev pull, and any diesel with a DPF fault is repaired before it is remapped.

name: Bracknell
intro: Petrol accounted for 61.3% of privately kept cars in the Bracknell Forest council area at the end of June 2026, and diesel for 23.8%, below England's 29.1%. Most private cars across the council area are petrol, then, and Stage 1 remapping works on the same settings in both fuels: it changes fuel, boost and timing in the engine's software, within its limits, and adds no parts. On a diesel, the gain is mid-range torque, which makes joining fast roads and overtaking easier. Any change in economy depends on how you drive and is modest. Tell your insurer about the remap once it is done.
driving: Welcome Break Fleet Services on the M3 is the closest listed service area, 14.3 km away, with Moto Reading Services on the M4 at 19.4 km. The M4 and the A329(M) are both on Bracknell's road list. Sandhurst (6.9 km) and Camberley (8.3 km) are a little further than Crowthorne, the closest at 4.6 km. In the 2021 Census, 46.3% of households in the Bracknell built-up area had two or more cars, against 35.4% across England and Wales. Census day fell in a lockdown, and 3.1% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, below the 4.4% for England and Wales. RG postcode MOT tests in 2025 had the Mercedes-Benz E Class fourth among diesel cars, and on an E Class the remap is felt most joining the M4.

name: Bradford

caz.name: Bradford Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers Bradford city centre and the outer ring road area and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: Bradford's Clean Air Zone, which covers the city centre and the outer ring road area, can charge vans but does not charge private cars. If you run a diesel van in the city, one point is worth knowing first: a remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the zone charges it. What Stage 1 remapping does change is how the engine responds. Nothing on the van is replaced: the fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within the engine's limits. The extra mid-range torque helps when you are loaded or towing, while the gearbox and clutch decide how far it can go. A van with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired first.
driving: Diesel is unusually common in the Bradford council area: 36.4% of privately kept cars, one of the highest shares of the 104 largest towns we cover, and their number fell only 1.6% over the year to June 2026. Main roads include the M606, A6177 and A658, and the nearest service area is Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62, about 9 km away. In the 2021 Census, 50.4% of working residents in the Bradford built-up area drove to work. In 2025 MOT tests across BD postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was by far the most tested diesel car, with the Audi A3 and BMW 3 Series next. On cars like these, a remap is about stronger pull through the gears and easier motorway joins.

name: Bradley Stoke
intro: Only 2.1 km separates Bradley Stoke from Patchway, and Filton and Stoke Gifford are 2.6 km away each, with Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne at 4.5 km. The town forms the northernmost part of the Bristol built-up area. For a car or van that tows a caravan or trailer, or often runs with a full load, Stage 1 remapping changes how the engine handles that weight. The remap alters the fuel, boost and timing settings through software, while keeping to the engine's limits. With something hitched behind, the extra mid-range torque on a diesel is the difference between holding a gear on a long drag and changing down.
driving: Four motorways are on Bradley Stoke's list of main roads, the M4, M5, M32 and M48, together with the A4174, A38, A4017 and A4018. Moto Severn View on the M48 is the nearest listed service area, 9.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 9.7% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales, and 10.6% of households had no car, against 23.3%. Petrol made up 64% of privately kept cars in the South Gloucestershire council area at the end of June 2026 and diesel 22.9%, below England's 29.1%. With petrol the council-wide majority, a remap may just as easily be for a turbo petrol.

name: Braintree
intro: Three in ten working residents of the Braintree built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, against 19% across England and Wales, and 8.2% went 30 km or more, against 4.4%. Those were lockdown figures, taken when fewer people were travelling to work. On longer runs, such as along the A120 and A131, a diesel with Stage 1 remapping overtakes more easily and needs fewer downshifts as traffic slows and speeds up again. No hardware is changed, the engine stays within its limits, and a remap does not alter the vehicle's emissions standard.
driving: Halstead, 8.9 km away, is the closest neighbouring town to Braintree, and Chelmsford is 16.7 km off. The nearest service area is Boreham Services on the A131, 14.4 km out, with Ardleigh South on the A120 at 29 km. In the 2021 Census, 56% of working residents drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Vans are a bigger part of the mix across the Braintree council area, with 91 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 across England. Across CM postcodes, 2025 MOT tests put the Ford Transit Custom second among diesel vans, behind the Transit. For a loaded Custom, low-rev torque is the useful gain, and the clutch sets the limit.

name: Brent
intro: Diesel is hanging on in Brent. Privately kept diesel cars in the Brent council area went from 12,884 to 12,516 in the year to June 2026, a fall of 2.9% and the 8th smallest among the 104 largest towns we cover. Diesel still accounts for 15.3% of the 82,039 private cars here. If you are keeping a diesel, a Stage 1 remap is one way to get more out of it without fitting anything. The gain you feel most is in the mid-range: more pull at the revs you actually use, so fewer changes down a gear. Your insurer has to be told about the remap.
driving: The M1, A406, A40 and A41 all appear among Brent's main roads, and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 8.1 km away. In the 2021 Census, 44.1% of households in the Brent council area had no car, and 21.7% of working residents drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales. In the council area, plug-ins make up 8.1% of private cars, one of the highest shares of the 104, and 92.8% of the 3,386 private vans are diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across HA postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van. As for the ULEZ, which can charge both cars and vans, a remap has no effect, because it does not alter a vehicle's emissions standard.

name: Brentwood
intro: Diesel is a smaller part of the car fleet in the Brentwood council area than across England: 19.9% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, against 29.1%, and the number of diesel cars fell 9.2% over the year, against 5.3%. Petrol made up 64.2%. That matters because Stage 1 remapping is not only a diesel job: the same software change to fuel, boost and timing settings is made on many petrol engines, always within the engine's limits. On a diesel, the gain people notice most is mid-range torque for easier overtaking. On either fuel, nothing is bolted on, and your insurer must be told about the remap.
driving: Brentwood lies just outside the M25, and the A12 and A127 are also among its main roads, with Moto Thurrock Services on the M25 14.9 km away. Havering is 7.8 km off and Billericay 8.6 km. In the 2021 Census, 35.2% of working residents in the Brentwood built-up area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 22.6% travelled 10 km or more, above the 19% figure. Both figures date from a lockdown census day. MOT tests in CM postcodes during 2025 had the Ford Transit Connect as the third most tested diesel van. For a car or van that mostly does M25 and A12 miles, a remap is about easier pulling at cruising speed, not a different vehicle.

name: Bridgend
