intro: Sarn Park services on the M4 is just 2.9 km from Bridgend, so the motorway is part of ordinary driving here rather than an occasional trip. The town also sits halfway between Cardiff and Swansea, 32 km from each, which puts both cities within easy reach. A mix of short local trips and steady M4 miles is where Stage 1 remapping on a diesel earns its place. The work is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, kept within what the engine was designed for, with no hardware added. What changes is the mid-range: joining from a slip road takes less effort, and overtaking at motorway speed needs fewer downshifts.
driving: Alongside the M4, the A48, A473 and A4061 are among Bridgend's main roads. Sarn is 4.2 km away, Pyle 8.4 km and Porthcawl 9.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 58.1% of working residents of the Bridgend built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 42% of households had two or more cars. Diesel is less common here than across Wales as a whole: it made up 31.1% of privately kept cars in the Bridgend council area at the end of June 2026, against 36.1%, and the number of diesel cars fell 6.1% over the year. In 2025 MOT tests across CF postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, and one working the M4 all day gets stronger pull from Stage 1.

name: Bridgwater
intro: Bridgwater has a motorway service area on its doorstep: Moto Bridgwater Services on the M5 is 2.3 km away, and two more M5 stops, Sedgemoor and Taunton Deane, sit 17.1 km and 19.2 km off. For a vehicle that uses the M5 often, Stage 1 remapping changes how the engine copes with motorway work. Only the software settings change, inside the engine's limits, and a diesel gains mid-range torque, so it holds a higher gear on gradients and passes slower traffic without dropping down. A vehicle with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired before any remap.
driving: In the 2021 Census, when a lockdown was in force, 55.4% of working residents in the Bridgwater built-up area drove to work and 25.8% travelled 10 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 19%. Burnham-on-Sea and Taunton are the nearest listed towns, at 13 km and 13.6 km. Vans are common across the Somerset council area, which had 127 privately kept vans per 1,000 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 in England. Alongside the M5, the A38 and A39 are on the town's road list, with Wellington (22.4 km) and Weston-super-Mare (24.7 km) further away. Pulling onto the M5, a remapped diesel reaches traffic speed with fewer gear changes.

name: Bridlington
intro: Bridlington is a long way from any service area: the nearest, Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, is 52.1 km away in a straight line, and the next two are 67.4 km and 75.8 km off. Even Driffield, the closest town listed, is 17.8 km away. Distances like these mean a car or van here covers long stretches between stops, and an engine with more pull in reserve is less tiring on those runs. That is the point of Stage 1 remapping: a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the gain is mid-range torque, so overtaking a slow vehicle takes less effort and fewer downshifts.
driving: Long commutes showed up in the 2021 Census too: 14.2% of working residents in the Bridlington built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and 54.8% drove to work. The main roads are the A165, A614 and A1038, and Scarborough is 22.8 km away. In the East Riding of Yorkshire council area, privately kept diesel cars fell 5.7% in the year to June 2026, a little faster than the 5.3% drop across England. In 2025 MOT tests across YO postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were the most tested diesel vans. With a full load on a long A-road run, a van's remap is felt as stronger pull at low revs, within the gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Brierley Hill
intro: Five towns lie within 4.2 km of Brierley Hill: Stourbridge at 3 km, Kingswinford at 3.3 km, Cradley Heath at 3.7 km, Dudley at 3.8 km and Halesowen at 4.2 km, all measured in a straight line. With neighbours that close, short trips between them are likely to be a large part of local driving, and that shapes what a Stage 1 remap should do here. The aim is a car that answers the throttle sooner in traffic, pulls away cleanly from lights and reaches the speed limit without working through every gear. A diesel showing a DPF warning is repaired before any remap goes on, and the remap itself stays within the engine's limits.
driving: Drivers heading for the M5 have Moto Frankley Services 8.6 km away; closer to home, the A461, A4036 and A491 are among Brierley Hill's main roads. In the 2021 Census, 59.3% of working residents in the Brierley Hill built-up area drove to work, well over the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 22.5% of households had no car, a little under the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. The Dudley council area had 75 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, fewer than England's 81. The Ford Transit Connect made the top five diesel vans in 2025 MOT tests across DY postcodes. On a loaded Transit Connect, a remap adds pull at low revs, but the clutch and gearbox still set the limit.

name: Brighouse
intro: Only 2.9 km separates Brighouse from Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62, measured in a straight line, and the M606 also appears among the town's main roads. With the motorway that close, a diesel here may spend a good part of its week at motorway speed, and that is where Stage 1 remapping changes how it feels. Merging from a slip road, overtaking and holding a gear on a long incline all become easier. The remap alters the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software and stays inside the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. Fuel use afterwards depends on how the vehicle is driven, and any change is modest, so stronger mid-range torque is what most drivers notice first.
driving: The town joins the M62 at junction 25, and the A644, A58, A629 and A62 are among its other main roads. Elland is 3.7 km away in a straight line and Huddersfield 6.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 53.6% of working residents in the Brighouse built-up area drove to work, and 35.4% of households had two or more cars, level with the England and Wales figure. In the Calderdale council area, privately kept diesel cars fell 6.1% in the year to June 2026, a steeper drop than England's 5.3%. In 2025 MOT tests across HD postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans and the Citroen Berlingo was also in the top five. A small van like the Berlingo pulls more easily with a load on board after a remap.

name: Brighton and Hove
intro: For every 1,000 privately kept cars in the Brighton and Hove council area at the end of June 2026, there were 92 private vans, the 4th highest ratio of the 104 largest towns we cover. Of those 8,112 vans, 92.8% were diesel. If you run one of them, think about Stage 1 remapping in terms of the load you carry. The extra torque sits in the mid-range, so a van that is often full or towing does more of its work without the driver reaching for a lower gear. Before any remap, the clutch and gearbox need to be in good order, because they set the limits.
driving: The A23 and A27 head the main road list, with the A259 and A270 alongside them, and Pyecombe Services on the A23 is 7.9 km away. Lewes is 8.5 km off. In the 2021 Census, only 25% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% for England and Wales, and 37.5% of households had no car. The council area had 87,807 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 63.3% petrol and 23.9% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BN postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, while the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the vans. For a car that uses the A23 or A27, Stage 1 makes joining faster traffic and overtaking easier.

name: Bristol

caz.name: Bristol Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers a small area of central Bristol and applies to cars and vans.

intro: Only 32% of working residents in the Bristol built-up area drove to work in the 2021 Census, far below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Diesel is thinning out too. In the Bristol council area, privately kept diesel cars fell 7.1% in the year to June 2026, one of the steepest falls of the 104 largest towns we cover, and diesel is now 19.4% of private cars. For the diesels that stay, Stage 1 remapping is a software job only: the fuel, boost and timing settings are changed within the engine's limits and nothing is bolted on. Most of the gain sits in the mid-range, which suits pulling away with a load or joining the M32.
driving: Bristol's Clean Air Zone, a Class D charging zone, covers a small area of central Bristol and applies to cars and vans. A remap does not alter a vehicle's emissions standard, so it does not change whether the zone charges it. Vans are common: the council area had 88 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, the 8th highest ratio of the 104, and 94.2% of its 15,784 vans were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BS postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were the most tested diesel vans. The nearest service area, Gordano on the M5, is 8.7 km away. For a working van, the torque gain helps most when loaded, within what the clutch can handle.

name: Broadstairs
intro: Ramsgate and Margate are 3 km and 3.6 km from Broadstairs, and the next town on the list, Deal, is 16.7 km away. Driving here mixes short hops between close neighbours with the occasional longer run out of Thanet. For Stage 1 remapping that matters in two ways. A diesel used mostly for short trips should be checked first, because any DPF, EGR or AdBlue fault is repaired before a remap goes on. And on the longer runs, the gain you feel is mid-range torque, so joining the A299 or passing slower traffic takes less effort. The remap itself is a software change to fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits.
driving: The A256, A299, A28, A255 and A254 are the main roads around Broadstairs, and no motorway is listed. Minster Services on the A299 is 7.7 km away, and the next, Whitfield on the A2, is 25.2 km. Two-car households were more common here than across Thanet at the 2021 Census: 36% of households in the Broadstairs built-up area had two or more cars, against 30.8% across the Thanet council area. The council area had 89 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 across England. The Vauxhall Vivaro and Citroen Berlingo were among the five most tested diesel vans at CT postcode MOT stations in 2025, and either one pulls more willingly from low revs after a remap.

name: Bromley
intro: Petrol accounts for 70.6% of the 137,106 privately kept cars in the Bromley council area, and diesel for just 12.2%, one of the lowest diesel shares of the 104 largest towns we cover. So in Bromley, Stage 1 remapping is more often about a petrol car than a diesel. The method is the same on both: the remap adjusts the fuel, boost and timing settings rather than adding parts, and stays within the engine's limits. On a petrol the result is a stronger, smoother response through the middle of the rev range. On a diesel it is more torque for overtaking and joining fast roads. Your insurer needs to be told either way.
driving: The council area has 6,181 privately kept vans, 89.4% of them diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across BR postcodes the Ford Transit and Ford Transit Custom were the two most tested diesel vans. For a van carrying a load, a remap's extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits. In the 2021 Census, only 22.9% of households in the council area had no car, close to the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, though just 27.9% of working residents drove to work. The nearest service area is RoadChef Clacket Lane on the M25, about 12 km away. The London ULEZ covers every borough and can charge cars and vans, and since a remap doesn't change the emissions standard, the charge is unaffected.

name: Bromsgrove
intro: Privately kept diesel cars in the Bromsgrove council area fell from 16,574 to 15,258 in the year to June 2026. That 7.9% drop is steeper than the 5.3% fall across England, and diesel is now 27.1% of private cars there. The diesels that remain still need looking after, and that comes before any Stage 1 remapping: a car with a DPF, EGR, AdBlue or injector fault is repaired first. Once the engine is healthy, the remap itself only alters software, the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside the engine's limits. What most drivers feel afterwards is stronger mid-range torque, so overtaking and climbing need fewer downshifts.
driving: For motorway runs from Bromsgrove, Hopwood Park Services on the M42 is 8.3 km away and Frankley, on the M5, 11.2 km, while the A491, A448 and A38 are the main A roads. Catshill lies 3.4 km off and Redditch 9.1 km. In the 2021 Census, 27.3% of working residents in the Bromsgrove built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales, and 45.4% of households had two or more cars. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter was the second most tested diesel van after the Ford Transit. A loaded Sprinter joining the M5 is where extra low-rev torque from a remap helps, within the limits of its gearbox.

name: Burgess Hill
intro: Ricebridge Services at Hickstead lies 4.4 km from Burgess Hill on the A23, and Pyecombe Services, 7.1 km away, is on the same road. For a diesel heading out onto the A23, the useful part of Stage 1 remapping is the extra torque from the middle of the rev range: the car gathers pace from a junction or a slip road without being held in a low gear, and a car carrying a family or a load feels less weighed down. Nothing is bolted on, and the remap stays within the engine's limits. Your insurer will need to know about it, so tell them before the work is done.
driving: The A272, A273 and A2300 also serve Burgess Hill. Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint is 3.4 km away, Haywards Heath 5.5 km, and Brighton and Hove and Lewes both about 13 km. In the 2021 Census, 43.9% of households in the Burgess Hill built-up area had two or more cars, against 35.4% for England and Wales, and 14.5% had none, against 23.3%. Across the Mid Sussex council area, 23% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, below England's 29.1%. In 2025 MOT tests across RH postcodes, the Volkswagen Caddy was the fourth most tested diesel van. A loaded small van like that feels a remap as extra pull away from junctions.

name: Burnley
intro: In the year to June 2026, the number of privately kept diesel cars in the Burnley council area dropped by only 2.8%, to 14,277, while across England it fell 5.3%. Diesel still made up 36.7% of privately kept cars there at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% for England. For people keeping a diesel on the road, Stage 1 remapping changes how the engine delivers its power without changing its parts: the fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, inside the engine's limits. What most drivers notice is stronger mid-range torque, which means easier overtaking, more confident joins onto the M65 and fewer downshifts.
driving: Hollin Bank Service Station is 4.1 km away on the M65, with the A56, A646 and A682 among the town's other main roads. Brierfield is 3.4 km away, and Nelson and Padiham 5.1 km each. In the 2021 Census, 55.3% of working residents in the Burnley built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, while 30.7% of households had no car, above the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. Among vans, diesel dominates: 97.3% of privately kept vans in the Burnley council area were diesel at the end of June 2026, compared with 94.2% across England. In 2025 MOT tests across BB postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter were the most tested diesel vans. Loaded or towing, vans like these gain low-rev pull from Stage 1.

name: Burntwood
intro: Chasetown, Chase Terrace, Boney Hay and Burntwood Green are all part of Burntwood, a town where most working residents drove to work in the 2021 Census. The figure for the Burntwood built-up area was 64.1%, against 54.9% across the Lichfield council area and 45.1% for England and Wales. Census day fell in a lockdown, so these are not today's figures, but the gap is a clear one. A car that does the daily run is the one where Stage 1 remapping is noticed most often, because the change is there every time you pull out of a junction or join a faster road. It is a software job, done within the engine's limits, with no extra parts.
driving: RoadChef Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll is 3.4 km from Burntwood, and the M6 Toll, A5, A5195 and A452 are among the town's main roads. Brownhills lies 3.8 km away and Lichfield 6.6 km. In the 2021 Census, only 13.2% of households in the built-up area had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales, and 46.7% had two or more. In the Lichfield council area, 28.6% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across WS postcodes, the Ford Focus was among the most tested diesel cars and the Vauxhall Vivaro among the vans. A Focus or Vivaro gains easier pull onto the M6 Toll from a remap.

name: Burton upon Trent
intro: Around Burton upon Trent, diesel still matters. In the East Staffordshire council area, 35.8% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% across England: about 23,400 cars, down from 24,636 a year earlier. A diesel is where the effect of Stage 1 remapping is simplest to describe. It gets more mid-range torque, so the car or van pulls harder from low revs and needs fewer downshifts with a load on board. A remap is a change the insurer must be told about, so speak to yours before the work goes ahead.
driving: The A38, A511, A444 and A5121 are among Burton upon Trent's main roads. The nearest services are on the A50: Derby with Burton at 8.9 km and Uttoxeter at 18.2 km. Swadlincote is the closest town at 6.3 km, and Derby is 17.2 km away. Long commutes were more common than average in the 2021 Census: 5.6% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more, against 4.4% across England and Wales. At the end of June 2026 the council area had 86 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, against 81 for England. Across DE postcodes, 2025 MOT tests counted more Ford Transits than any other diesel van, with the Volkswagen Transporter next, and a remap helps either pull a load, within the gearbox's limits.

name: Bury
intro: Three motorways, the M60, M62 and M66, are among Bury's main roads, alongside the A56 and A58. Mixing town streets with motorway miles is the kind of use Stage 1 remapping suits. Nothing is bolted on: the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within the engine's limits. On a diesel the gain is mid-range torque: the car joins the M66 or M60 with less effort, holds its gear for longer when traffic slows, and overtakes without a long run-up. Your insurer must be told about a remap.
driving: Birch Services on the M62 is 5.1 km away, and Radcliffe is 3.9 km, Heywood 4.6 km and Ramsbottom 4.9 km. BL8 and BL9 are the town's postcode districts. The 2021 Census found 23.3% of households in the Bury built-up area without a car, the same as the England and Wales figure. In the Bury council area, diesel made up 27.8% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, a little below England's 29.1%, and their number fell 6.7% over the year, against England's 5.3%. In 2025 MOT tests across BL postcodes, the Ford Transit Custom was among the five most tested diesel vans. With a load on, a Transit Custom gains low-rev pull from a remap, within its clutch limits.

name: Bury St Edmunds
intro: The nearest service area to Bury St Edmunds is Beacon Hill Services on the A140, 27.5 km away, and the closest one on the A14 is further still, at 34 km. Distances like that point to a lot of steady A-road driving, the kind a Stage 1 remap on a diesel suits well. Nothing is fitted to the car; the change is to the software that controls fuel, boost and timing, and it stays within the engine's limits. That adds mid-range torque, so the engine responds more readily on a single carriageway and can hold its pace on a rise with fewer gear changes.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 7.1% of working residents in the Bury St Edmunds built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and 50.7% drove. Thetford is 18.7 km away, Stowmarket 20.6 km and Newmarket 20.7 km, and the A143, A134 and A1302 are listed alongside the A14. In the West Suffolk council area, 34.8% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, above England's 29.1%. In 2025 MOT tests across IP postcodes, the Ford Ranger was among the five most tested diesel vans, alongside the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter. A Ranger towing a trailer feels a Stage 1 remap as stronger low-rev pull, and the insurer has to be told.

name: Bushey
intro: Bushey recorded relatively few households without a car at the 2021 Census: 12.6% in the Bushey built-up area, against 15.5% across the Hertsmere council area and 23.3% in England and Wales. At the other end, 44.3% of households had two or more cars, well above the England and Wales figure of 35.4%. With a car on nearly every drive, the questions people ask about Stage 1 remapping are practical ones: what changes, and what does not. Only the software does. The engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted within its limits, and no parts are added. On a diesel you feel stronger mid-range torque when pulling out onto the M1. A car with an EGR or injector fault is repaired before it is remapped.
driving: Watford is Bushey's closest neighbour, 3.3 km away, and Harrow is 6.5 km off. The town spans five WD postcode districts: WD17, WD18, WD19, WD23 and WD24. London Gateway Services, 6.8 km away on the M1, is the nearest listed service area. Bushey Heath, on the south-east side of town, reaches 165 metres above sea level. In the 2021 Census, 40.8% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. At the end of June 2026 the Hertsmere council area had just 48 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, against 81 in England. The Mercedes-Benz E Class topped the diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across WD postcodes, and remapped, it takes the climb to Bushey Heath with fewer downshifts.

name: Caerphilly
intro: More than a fifth of working residents in the Caerphilly built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census: 22.6%, above the England and Wales figure of 19%. Only 2.5% went 30 km or more, against 4.4%, so most of the longer commutes fell between 10 km and 30 km. That middle band, longer than the 9 km hop to Cardiff but short of a long-distance run, is where Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is felt day to day. The change to fuel, boost and timing is made in software, inside the engine's limits, and lifts torque in the middle of the rev range, so climbs and merging into traffic take less effort.
driving: The M4, A470 and A468 are among Caerphilly's main roads, along with the A469, A4054 and A473, and two motorway service areas are close: Cardiff Gate at 8 km and Cardiff West at 9.5 km. The town lies at the southern end of the Rhymney Valley, with Church Village 6.9 km away and Ystrad Mynach 7.8 km. Diesel held 36.6% of privately kept cars in the Caerphilly council area at the end of June 2026, slightly above the Wales figure of 36.1%, although the count fell from 33,942 to 32,191 over the year. The Ford Kuga was among the five most tested diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across CF postcodes. For a Kuga pulling a trailer, the extra mid-range from a remap is what you notice.

name: Camberley
intro: Surrey Heath lost 7.9% of its privately kept diesel cars in the year to June 2026, the count falling from 13,469 to 12,402, a faster drop than the 5.3% across England. Diesel is now 22.8% of private cars in the council area, which includes Camberley, against 29.1% for England. For anyone holding on to a diesel, Stage 1 remapping works with what is already under the bonnet: a software change to fuel, boost and timing, inside the engine's limits. The difference shows in the mid-range, with stronger pull for overtaking and fewer gear changes on hills. Before any remap, faults such as a blocked DPF or a failing EGR valve are repaired first.
driving: Sandhurst, 3.9 km away, and Frimley, at 2.4 km, are Camberley's nearest neighbours, and Yateley is 7.3 km off. The M3 is on the town's road list with the A30, A322, A325 and A331, and the closest service area is Welcome Break Fleet on the M3, 10 km away. Car ownership is high: in the 2021 Census, 52.3% of households in the Camberley built-up area had two or more cars, against 35.4% across England and Wales, though the Surrey Heath council area as a whole was higher still at 55.8%. Vans are scarcer, with 59 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars in the Surrey Heath council area at the end of June 2026, below England's 81.

name: Cambridge
intro: In Cambridge, the car was not how most people got to work. In the 2021 Census, just 19.8% of working residents in the Cambridge built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 33.9% of households had no car. Trips out of the city are where performance counts: Cambourne is 14.1 km away, Newmarket 19.1 km, and the M11 is among the main roads. That is where a Stage 1 remap shows. On a diesel, stronger mid-range torque makes overtaking and joining faster roads easier, from a change to the engine's software settings made within its limits.
driving: Other main roads include the A14, A10 and A428, and the nearest listed service areas are Four Went Ways on the A11, 10.5 km away, and Cambridge Services on the A14 at 12.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 19.3% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars. Of the 40,356 privately kept cars in the Cambridge council area at the end of June 2026, 26.5% were diesel and 57.6% petrol, and private diesel cars fell from 11,391 to 10,702 over the year. Across CB postcodes in 2025 MOT tests, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter. A loaded van benefits from extra torque, though the gearbox and clutch set the limits.

name: Cambuslang
intro: In Scotland's 2022 Census, 37.9% of households in the Cambuslang locality had two or more cars, compared with 30.5% across Scotland. Only 21% had no car, below the Scottish 26.4%. Where one of a household's cars is a diesel, Stage 1 remapping is a way to make it more responsive without changing any hardware. The work adjusts the fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine's software and stays within its limits. What you feel is stronger mid-range torque: less need to change down on a hill, and easier overtaking. Once it is done, tell your insurer, because a remap counts as a modification.
driving: RoadChef Bothwell Services is 5.8 km from Cambuslang on the M74, and the M73 is on the town's road list as well. Viewpark is also 5.8 km away, and Hamilton 7.8 km. Few working residents in the locality travelled 30 km or more to work in Scotland's 2022 Census: 3.2%, against 4.9% for Scotland. The South Lanarkshire council area lost 11.2% of its privately kept diesel cars in the year to June 2026, more than the 9.2% fall across Scotland. In 2025 MOT tests across G postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter was the second most tested diesel van after the Ford Transit. For a loaded Sprinter heading onto the M74, extra low-rev pull helps, within what the clutch and gearbox can take.

name: Camden
intro: Just 12.3% of privately kept cars in the Camden council area ran on diesel at the end of June 2026, the 4th lowest share of the 104 largest towns we cover. That is 4,217 diesel cars, down from 4,442 a year earlier, while petrol made up 64.2%. For the owners of those diesels, Stage 1 remapping brings more mid-range torque, the pull that makes joining faster roads and overtaking easier. It comes from software changes to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. A car with a DPF or injector fault is repaired before it is remapped.
driving: Camden sits inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which covers all London boroughs and can charge cars and vans a daily fee. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the ULEZ charges yours. In the 2021 Census, just 6.9% of working residents in the council area drove to work, and 63.6% of households had no car. Plug-in cars made up 12.8% of private cars in June 2026, the 2nd highest share of the 104. The M1 is on the main road list, and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 11.8 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across NW postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested van.

name: Cannock
intro: Within 6.9 km of Cannock there are three places to stop on a longer drive: The Trucker's Rest on the A5 at 4.1 km, RoadChef Norton Canes on the M6 Toll at 4.7 km and Moto Hilton Park on the M6 at 6.9 km. With the A5, the M6 and the M6 Toll that close, many trips out of Cannock can begin on a slip road, which is the easiest place to feel what Stage 1 remapping does. A diesel gains mid-range torque, so pulling into fast traffic takes less effort and fewer gear changes. The change is software only: fuel, boost and timing are adjusted, the engine's limits are respected and nothing is fitted.
driving: Cars dominated the commute in the 2021 Census, when 64.1% of working residents in the Cannock built-up area drove to work, compared with 45.1% across England and Wales. Great Wyrley and Cheslyn Hay is 4.5 km away, Burntwood 6.2 km and Brownhills 7.9 km, and the A34, A460 and A4601 are among the local main roads. The Cannock Chase council area had 102 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 across England, and 96% of those vans were diesel. Among diesel vans given an MOT at WS-postcode test stations in 2025, the Ford Transit came first and the Volkswagen Transporter second. For a van working loaded, extra pull at low revs means fewer downshifts, provided the clutch is in good order.

name: Canterbury
intro: With 32.9% of households in the Canterbury built-up area having no car in the 2021 Census, the city sits well above the 23.3% across England and Wales. Only 33.7% of working residents drove to work, a figure from a census taken in lockdown. On the A2, which is on the city's road list, the mid-range torque from Stage 1 remapping is what you feel when overtaking. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Any existing fault, from a sticking EGR valve to a worn injector, is repaired before the remap goes on.
driving: The city's listed neighbours run from Whitstable at 8.7 km out to Ashford at 20.9 km. The A28, A257, A290 and A291 are on the road list with the A2, and Stop24 Folkestone Services on the M20 is 20.6 km off. Just under a fifth of working residents in the built-up area, 19.5%, travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, a shade above the 19% for England and Wales. In the Canterbury council area, the fall in privately kept diesel cars over the year to June 2026 was 4.4%, smaller than the 5.3% across England. In 2025 MOT tests across CT postcodes, the Ford Kuga was among the five most tested diesel cars. For a Kuga towing a trailer on the A28, the extra torque is what you notice.

name: Canvey Island
intro: Bridges over the creeks link Canvey Island to the Essex mainland, and in the 2021 Census 56.2% of working residents in the Canvey Island built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. That figure comes from a census day in lockdown, when commuting was below its usual level. When most journeys begin with the same run off the island, Stage 1 remapping is felt early in the drive: stronger mid-range pull joining the A130 and fewer downshifts in slow traffic. Nothing is bolted on, and a remap leaves the vehicle's emissions standard as it was.
driving: Southend-on-Sea is 9 km from Canvey Island and Stanford-le-Hope 8.9 km. Orsett Cock Services on the A13, 12.4 km away, is the closest place to stop. In the 2021 Census, 7.7% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales. Vans are a little more common in the Castle Point council area than across England: 88 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81. Among diesel vans at SS postcode MOT stations in 2025, the Ford Transit was tested far more than any other. For a Transit carrying tools or materials, a remap adds pull from low revs, and how far it goes depends on the gearbox and clutch.

name: Cardiff
intro: With the M4, A470 and A48 among its main roads, the Welsh capital mixes city driving with quick motorway access: Cardiff Gate Services is 6 km away and Cardiff West 8.3 km. Stage 1 remapping suits that mix. In town, a diesel pulls more cleanly from low revs. On the M4 or the A470, a slip-road join or an overtake feels less strained thanks to the extra mid-range torque, and you stay in a higher gear for longer. The engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits. Nothing is bolted on, and the vehicle keeps the emissions standard it had before.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 39.9% of working residents in the Cardiff built-up area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 26.5% of households had no car. Neighbouring towns are close: Penarth is 6.4 km away, Caerphilly 9 km and Barry 11.4 km. In the Cardiff council area, 29.1% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, and so were 96.3% of the 9,789 private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across CF postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf, Ford Focus and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars, while the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the vans. driving: Driving to work was common in Derby in the 2021 Census: 50.2% of working residents in the built-up area drove, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 18.5% travelled 10 km or more. The A38, A50 and A52 are among the main roads, with the A6, A61 and A516, and the two closest service areas are both on the A50, Derby South at 8.2 km and Derby with Burton at 8.4 km. In 2025 MOT tests across DE postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans, ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter and Vauxhall Vivaro. The council area had 7,088 private vans, 95.6% of them diesel. On A-road commutes, a remap's extra torque mainly means fewer gear changes.

name: Derry

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021, during a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual. NISRA settlement figures are approximated from small areas; workers exclude full-time students, and distance bands count work within Northern Ireland only.

intro: Diesel still leads by a wide margin in the Derry City and Strabane council area: 66.1% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 52.7% across Northern Ireland. The number barely moved over the year, from 49,848 to 49,449, a fall of 0.8% against 2.1% for Northern Ireland as a whole. If yours is one of those diesels, Stage 1 remapping adjusts the fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits. The gain you notice is mid-range torque: easier overtaking, firmer pull with a trailer and fewer downshifts on hills. A diesel with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired first.
driving: The nearest service area to Derry, Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6, is 41.2 km away, and the main roads are the A2, A5, A6, A40, A514 and A515. Strabane is 21.9 km off and Limavady 23.6 km. In the 2021 Census, only 6.6% of working residents in the Derry City settlement travelled 10 km or more to work, against 25.6% across Northern Ireland, but that count leaves out work outside Northern Ireland, and the city sits close to the border with County Donegal. Car ownership was lower too: 30.9% of households had no car or van, against 19.5%. The council area had 116 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, above Northern Ireland's 98. For a loaded van on a long A6 run, extra torque means fewer downshifts.

name: Dewsbury
intro: Households in Dewsbury were less likely to run two or more cars than those across England and Wales at the 2021 Census: 31.6% in the built-up area, against 35.4%, while 26.5% had no car at all. Where a household has one car, it has to do everything, from the commute to the weekend load, so any Stage 1 remapping needs to suit all of it. On a diesel the benefit is torque in the middle of the rev range: easier joins onto faster roads, more confident overtaking and fewer downshifts when the car is full. Nothing is added to the engine, and its emissions standard stays the same, but your insurer must be told about the remap.
driving: In the Kirklees council area, 31.9% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% in England. In the 2021 Census, 54.9% of working residents in the Dewsbury built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Five postcode districts cover the town, WF5, WF12, WF13, WF16 and WF17, and Ossett and Heckmondwike are each 3.9 km away in a straight line. Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62 is 8 km off and Moto Woolley Edge on the M1 9 km. In 2025 MOT tests across WF postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf, Ford Focus and BMW 3 Series were the most tested diesel cars, and on any of them a remap shows as stronger in-gear pull.

name: Didcot
intro: Didcot's main roads are the A34, A4130, A417, A4185 and A415, and none of them is a motorway. On roads like these, a stronger response through the middle of the rev range can make a diesel feel less laboured, and that is where Stage 1 remapping usually makes its difference. The change is made in software to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and nothing is added to the engine. You get firmer pull without needing to drop a gear. Fuel economy may change a little, depending on how the vehicle is driven, but it should not be the reason for a remap.
driving: Oxford is 16.2 km from Didcot, with Abingdon-on-Thames closer at 7.7 km. Every listed service area is some way out: Welcome Break Oxford on the M40 at 17.5 km, Moto Chieveley on the M4 at 18.5 km and Peartree on the A44 at 20.6 km. In the 2021 Census, 20% of working residents in the Didcot built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, slightly above the 19% for England and Wales. The South Oxfordshire council area had 81 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, level with England. In 2025, 40% of cars and small vans given an MOT at OX postcode stations were diesel.

name: Doncaster
intro: Diesel makes up 41% of privately kept cars in the Doncaster council area, against 29.1% across England, on figures for the end of June 2026, while petrol accounts for 45.3%, compared with 57.6% in England. For the many people still running a diesel, Stage 1 remapping is a way to get more from the engine they already own rather than changing the car. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, held within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. The gain shows up as mid-range torque, which helps when joining the M18 or the A1(M) and when overtaking. Any change in fuel use depends on how the car is driven and is modest.
driving: Bentley is 3.8 km from Doncaster in a straight line, Armthorpe 4.6 km and New Rossington and Rossington 5.2 km, and the A638, A18, A630 and A19 are also among the main roads. The nearest services are Moto Doncaster (North) on the M180, 11.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 4.8% of working residents in the Doncaster built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, a little above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, while 30.4% of households had no car. In 2025 MOT tests across DN postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, with the Vauxhall Vivaro second. A Vivaro or Transit doing long runs with weight on board gains easier pull from a remap, provided it respects the gearbox and clutch.

name: Dover
intro: Households without a car made up 29.4% of the Dover built-up area in the 2021 Census, more than the 23.3% for England and Wales and the 20.1% across the Dover council area. Two-car households were less common too, at 27.4% against 35.4% for England and Wales. A household's only car has to do every job, from the shopping to the longer trips. For a diesel doing all of that, Stage 1 remapping changes the fuel, boost and timing settings through software, inside the engine's limits, without fitting anything. The benefit is stronger mid-range torque: smoother pulling away, easier climbs and less need to change down. If you go ahead, your insurer must be told.
driving: Whitfield Services on the A2 is only 2.6 km from Dover, but the next nearest, Stop24 Folkestone Services on the M20, is 18.5 km away. The A2 and A20 head the road list of this major ferry port. Journeys to work of 10 km or more were made by 26.8% of working residents in the built-up area in the 2021 Census, compared with 19% for England and Wales. The Dover council area counted 93 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, above England's 81. In 2025 MOT tests across CT postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars. A Qashqai with a full boot or a loaded van holds its gear better with the extra pull.

name: Droitwich Spa
intro: Of the working residents counted in the Droitwich Spa built-up area in the 2021 Census, 6.3% travelled 30 km or more to work, measured in a straight line, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and 24.2% went 10 km or more. Longer regular journeys like these are where Stage 1 remapping is easiest to appreciate, because the engine spends so much of its time pulling at a steady load. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. On a diesel, the difference you notice is extra mid-range torque: overtaking takes less planning, slip roads are easier and the car holds a higher gear for longer.
driving: The M5 is among Droitwich Spa's main roads, with the A38 and A449, but services are further off: Hopwood Park on the M42 is 18.1 km away and Moto Frankley on the M5 20.7 km. Worcester is 8.2 km away in a straight line. The 2021 Census found 44.1% of households in the built-up area with two or more cars, against 35.4% in England and Wales. The Wychavon council area had 100 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 in England. In 2025 MOT tests across WR postcodes, the Volkswagen Transporter was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Ford Transit. Loaded, a Transporter gains stronger low-rev pull from Stage 1, within its gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Dudley
intro: Plenty of Dudley households manage without a car. In the 2021 Census, 27.8% of households in the Dudley built-up area had none, above both the England and Wales figure of 23.3% and the 20.5% for the Dudley council area, and only 30.9% had two or more. Where a home has just one car, that car tends to do everything: the commute, the shopping and the weekend trip with a full boot. For a car with that much to do, Stage 1 remapping that stays within the engine's limits matters more than chasing figures. Software is all that changes, nothing is bolted on, and the gain you notice is easier mid-range pull with passengers and luggage aboard.
driving: The M5 is the only motorway among Dudley's main roads, which also include the A461, A4123 and A41, and Moto Frankley Services on it is 9.8 km away. Rowley Regis, at 3.4 km, is the nearest place to Dudley, and Cradley Heath is 4 km away. Driving was how 57.4% of working residents in the built-up area got to work in the 2021 Census, against 45.1% across England and Wales. At the end of June 2026, 29.1% of privately kept cars in the Dudley council area were diesel, the same share as across England. Of the diesel cars given an MOT across DY postcodes in 2025, the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus were the most common, and in either a remap is felt pulling out of junctions.

name: Dumfries
intro: For every 1,000 privately kept cars in the Dumfries and Galloway council area, there were 142 private vans at the end of June 2026, well above the Scotland figure of 84, and 96% of those vans were diesel. A working van is where Stage 1 remapping is most practical, because the gain is in pulling power rather than top speed. The change is made in software, to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Extra mid-range torque helps a loaded van pull away and hold its speed on hills. Gearbox and clutch limits still matter, so the remap has to suit the whole van, not just the engine.
driving: All eight main roads on the Dumfries list are A roads, among them the A75, A76 and A701. The nearest service areas are on the A74(M): Annandale Water Services at 21 km and Welcome Break Gretna Green Services at 34.2 km, and Carlisle is 46.9 km away. In Scotland's 2022 Census, 52% of working residents in the Dumfries locality drove to work, above the 45.9% for Scotland, yet only 12.5% travelled 10 km or more. In 2025 MOT tests across DG postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, and the Mitsubishi L200 and Toyota Hilux were both in the top five. For an L200 or Hilux with a trailer on, the extra torque is the part of a remap you would notice.

name: Dundee

caz.name: Dundee Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers the area inside the A991 Inner Ring Road and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Inside the A991 Inner Ring Road, Dundee's Low Emission Zone applies to both cars and vans. It works by penalty charge, with no option to pay to enter, and the Bell Street, West Marketgait NCP and Wellgate car parks are left out. If you are thinking about Stage 1 remapping on a diesel, the zone is not affected either way: a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it can't change whether a vehicle is charged. What changes is how the engine pulls. The remap works on fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits, and the result is more mid-range torque for overtaking and hills.
driving: Privately kept diesel cars in the Dundee City council area fell from 14,571 to 13,251 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 9.1% and one of the steepest of the 104 largest towns we cover. Diesel is still 23.7% of private cars, and there are 3,173 privately kept vans, 97.1% of them diesel. The A90 is on the main road list, with Forfar Services on the A90 about 18 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across DD postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van by a wide margin, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. For those keeping a diesel, a remap adds pull on the A90, and a loaded van gains torque within its gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Dunfermline
intro: Motorway access is part of the Dunfermline road picture: the M90 and the A823(M) are both on the list, alongside A roads such as the A92, A907 and A985. For a diesel that regularly uses the M90, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about mid-range pull: getting up to speed on a slip road and passing slower traffic with less effort. The remap changes fuel, boost and timing in software, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Any change in fuel use is modest and depends on your driving. Before a remap, a vehicle showing a fault, such as a DPF, EGR or injector problem, needs to be repaired.
driving: Moto Kinross Services, 15.6 km away on the M90, is the nearest service area, and Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 22.6 km off. The nearest listed neighbour is Rosyth at 3.7 km, with South Queensferry at 9.5 km and Linlithgow at 14.9 km. In Scotland's 2022 Census, 24.2% of working residents in the Dunfermline locality travelled 10 km or more, above the 20.4% for Scotland, and 34.9% of households had two or more cars, against 30.5%. Across the whole Fife council area, 29.3% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across KY postcodes, the Kia Sportage was among the five most tested diesel cars, and for an SUV like that, extra torque helps most when towing.

name: Dunstable
intro: Dunstable sits at the western edge of the urban area it shares with Houghton Regis, just 2.5 km away, and Luton, 7.4 km off. Driving here mixes built-up traffic with the M1, which is among the town's main roads, and Stage 1 remapping suits that mix. On a diesel, extra mid-range torque makes pulling away and merging easier, with fewer downshifts in slow traffic. Your insurer must be told about the remap, as with any modification. It does not alter the vehicle's emissions standard, and any fault, such as a DPF or AdBlue problem, is repaired first.
driving: Toddington Services on the M1 is 7.2 km from Dunstable, and the A5 and A505 are also among its main roads. Leighton Buzzard is 9.8 km away. In the 2021 Census, 53.5% of working residents in the Dunstable built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 17% of households had no car, against 23.3%. In the Central Bedfordshire council area, 26.7% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, below the 29.1% across England. In 2025 MOT tests across LU postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter was the second most tested diesel van after the Ford Transit. On a loaded Sprinter or Transit, low-rev torque is the useful gain, and the van's clutch and gearbox set the limit.

name: Durham
intro: The A1(M) is on Durham's road list, along with the A690, A691, A167, A177, A181 and A688, so faster roads are within easy reach of DH1. Out on those roads, a Stage 1 remap shows itself with a full car: passengers and luggage on board, and the diesel still pulls without a string of downshifts. Only the engine's software settings for fuel, boost and timing are revised, within the engine's limits, and no parts are fitted. The extra torque sits in the mid-range, which is where overtaking happens. Insurers have to be told about a remap.
driving: Fewer working residents drove to work in the Durham built-up area than across the County Durham council area as a whole at the 2021 Census: 41%, against 57.4% for the council area and 45.1% for England and Wales, while 24.6% travelled 10 km or more. Durham Services on the A1(M) is 6.9 km away and Easington on the A19 13.9 km. Chester-le-Street is 8.1 km off and Spennymoor 8.7 km. The council area had 96 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 in England. For a van loaded most days, a Stage 1 remap adds pull at low revs, within what the clutch and gearbox can handle.

name: Ealing
intro: The M4 and the A40 both appear among Ealing's main roads, and Moto Heston Services on the M4 is just 5 km away. Yet the car on an Ealing driveway is far more often petrol than diesel: 65.8% of the 105,587 privately kept cars in the council area ran on petrol at the end of June 2026, against 15.1% on diesel. A Stage 1 remap is not only for diesels: on a petrol car, the same kind of engine settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits. On a diesel, the gain most drivers notice is mid-range torque, the pull you use when joining the M4 or overtaking.
driving: Other main roads include the A406 and A312, and Hounslow is 6.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 24.5% of working residents in the Ealing council area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 36.8% of households had no car. Vans are relatively few in the council area: 4,219, or 40 for every 1,000 private cars, one of the lowest ratios of the 104 largest towns we cover. In 2025 MOT tests across W postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. Ealing sits within the ULEZ like every London borough. Its daily charge can apply to cars and vans, and because a remap leaves the emissions standard alone, it makes no difference to whether you pay.

name: East Grinstead
intro: East Grinstead's nearest neighbouring towns are a fair distance off. Horley is 11.6 km away in a straight line, Crawley 11.7 km and Oxted 13.2 km, with Crowborough and Haywards Heath further still. Trips to them are proper drives rather than quick hops, and a good share of the mileage is done at a steady pace on A roads. Stage 1 remapping is noticed on driving like that. It alters the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits, without adding any parts. On a diesel the gain is mid-range torque, which shows when you overtake on an open stretch or climb with passengers and luggage aboard.
driving: The A22 and A264 are the town's two main roads, and the nearest motorway services, Moto Pease Pottage on the M23, are 13.8 km away, with RoadChef Clacket Lane on the M25 at 16.5 km. In the 2021 Census, 22.6% of working residents in the East Grinstead built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work and 5.4% went 30 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 19% and 4.4%. Only 13.9% of households had no car. Across the Mid Sussex council area, privately kept diesel cars fell 6.7% over the year to June 2026, faster than England's 5.3%. For a diesel doing regular A22 runs, a remap mainly makes overtaking quicker and cleaner.

name: East Kilbride
intro: Nearly a quarter of working residents in the East Kilbride locality travelled 10 km or more to work in Scotland's 2022 Census: 23.8%, against 20.4% across Scotland. There is no motorway on the town's own road list, which is made up of the A726, A725, A749, A727 and A730. For a diesel driven on A roads like these, much of its work happens in the mid-range: pulling out to overtake, picking up after a junction, holding speed on a hill. Stage 1 remapping is a software-only change aimed at that mid-range, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive, and it should not be the reason for doing it.
driving: Of the places listed around East Kilbride, Giffnock is the furthest, 8.3 km away. The two nearest service areas are level at 9.9 km: RoadChef Bothwell and RoadChef Hamilton, both on the M74, with the M74 Truck Stop further out at 22.1 km. Fewer households in the locality were without a car than across Scotland as a whole: 23.3% against 26.4% in Scotland's 2022 Census. Privately kept vans are scarcer in the South Lanarkshire council area: 68 per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 84 across Scotland. The BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz A Class were among the most tested diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across G postcodes. On a diesel A Class, the extra mid-range torque is what you notice pulling out onto the A725 or A726.

name: Eastbourne
intro: After Polegate Services, 5.4 km away on the A22, the next listed service area for Eastbourne is Pyecombe Services on the A23, 34.2 km off, with Ricebridge Services at Hickstead 38.7 km away. With no motorway on the town's road list, longer trips mean A-road runs, and that is the kind of driving where Stage 1 remapping is felt. The remap is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, done within the engine's limits. On a diesel, extra mid-range torque makes passing slower traffic and climbing hills easier, with fewer downshifts. Fuel use may shift slightly with driving style, and insurers must be told about a remap.
driving: The A22, A259 and A27 are the main roads, along with the A2280 and A2290. Polegate is 4.2 km away, Hailsham 8.5 km and Bexhill-on-Sea 13.1 km. Trips to work tended to stay local in the 2021 Census: 15.3% of working residents in the built-up area went 10 km or more, below the England and Wales figure of 19%. In the Eastbourne council area, diesel was 24.2% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, under England's 29.1%, while petrol hybrids made up 8.8%. Of the diesel cars given an MOT across BN postcodes in 2025, the Volkswagen Golf, Nissan Qashqai and BMW 3 Series were the most tested. On short local runs, a Golf or Qashqai feels the remap as quicker response at low revs.

name: Eastleigh
intro: Chandler's Ford is 3.8 km from Eastleigh, West End 4.8 km, Hedge End 6.4 km and Southampton 6.5 km. Trips that short may not let a diesel's DPF get hot enough to clear itself, which is why Stage 1 remapping is only carried out once any fault there, or with the AdBlue, EGR or injectors, has been repaired. The remap itself changes fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine software, within the engine's limits. On short runs, the extra mid-range torque means pulling away from junctions and roundabouts with less revving and fewer gear changes. Fuel use changes only a little, depending on how you drive.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 50% of working residents in the Eastleigh built-up area drove to work, above the 45.1% for England and Wales. The town lies on the River Itchen, and the A3035 and A335 are among its main roads, with the M3 and M27 also listed. The closest service area, at Rownhams on the M27, is 7.8 km away. At the end of June 2026 the Eastleigh council area had 83 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, slightly above England's 81, and 94.6% of them were diesel. SO postcode MOT tests in 2025 had the Ford Transit, Volkswagen Transporter and Ford Transit Custom as the most tested diesel vans. A van remap must respect the gearbox and clutch, and is felt most with a full load.

name: Eccles
intro: The M602 cuts right through Eccles, and the M60, M62 and M61 sit on the town's road list beside it. A slip road is rarely far away for drivers here, so the useful part of Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is confident merging and easier overtaking at motorway speed, rather than outright pace. The remap changes the fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine's software, staying within its limits, and nothing is bolted on. The gain you feel is mid-range torque, so the car pulls harder from low revs and holds a gear for longer. Any change to fuel economy is modest and comes down to how you drive.
driving: Of the neighbouring places, Worsley is closest to Eccles at 2.5 km, then Swinton at 2.9 km and Urmston at 3.6 km, and the A57, A572 and A576 are among the local A roads. The nearest service area, Moto Birch on the M62, is 12.7 km away. In the 2021 Census, 33.1% of households in the Eccles built-up area had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales, and only 23.7% had two or more. In the Salford council area, 28.9% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, just under England's 29.1%. Where one car does every job in a household, a remap that makes it easier to drive in town and on the motorway alike is the usual aim.

name: Edinburgh

caz.name: Edinburgh Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers the city centre and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Private diesel cars in the City of Edinburgh council area fell from 38,167 to 34,481 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 9.7% and the 2nd biggest fall of the 104 largest towns we cover. Diesel now makes up 19.9% of the 173,168 privately kept cars there. For drivers who are keeping a diesel, Stage 1 remapping is a way to change how it drives without changing the car. The remap is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, and the gain you notice is mid-range torque. A car with a DPF, AdBlue, EGR or injector fault is repaired before any remap.
driving: The Edinburgh Low Emission Zone covers the city centre, including Tollcross, Queen Street, Picardy Place, Abbeyhill and the Meadows. It applies to cars and vans through penalty charges, with no option to pay to enter. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it doesn't change how the zone treats yours. Away from the centre, the A720 and A8 are on the main road list, Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 4.8 km away, and Moto Musselburgh Services on the A1 is 9.5 km. The council area had 9,239 private vans in June 2026, 93.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across EH postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans and the Volkswagen Golf the cars, with the Land Rover Discovery second.

name: Egham
intro: Junction 13 of the M25 is Egham's link to the motorway network, and the M3 also appears on the town's list of main roads, with the A30, A308 and A320. For a car that spends time on those roads, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about how it joins traffic and overtakes at speed. The work changes fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. On a diesel the gain you notice is mid-range torque, so a slip road onto the M25 takes less effort and the car needs fewer downshifts. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive and is modest, so treat it as a side effect rather than the reason to do it.
driving: Staines-upon-Thames is 4.1 km from Egham, Chertsey 5.6 km and Ascot 7.2 km, so plenty of journeys are short. None of the listed service areas is close: Moto Heston on the M4 is 13.7 km away and Wisley on the A3 15.7 km. In the 2021 Census, 39.6% of working residents in the Egham built-up area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, though census day fell in a lockdown. Diesel was 20.3% of privately kept cars in the Runnymede council area at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% across England. At TW postcode MOT stations in 2025, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and C Class were the two most tested diesel cars, and on either one Stage 1 brings smoother, stronger pull from low revs.

name: Elgin
intro: With Elgin Services 2.9 km away on the A96, the town has a service area close by, but the next one, Ashgrove Services on the same road, is 32.4 km off. The A96 and the A941 are the two main roads listed for Elgin, and neither is a motorway. On roads like these, a diesel with more mid-range torque gets past slower traffic in less time and holds its gear on hills, which is the point of Stage 1 remapping. The engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within its limits, and no parts are bolted on. Your insurer needs to know about the change.
driving: Nairn is 34.2 km from Elgin. In Scotland's 2022 Census, 50.6% of working residents in the Elgin locality drove to work, above the Scotland figure of 45.9%, and 31.6% of households had two or more cars, slightly more than the 30.5% for Scotland. Diesel still made up 34% of privately kept cars in the Moray council area at the end of June 2026, above the 27.7% for Scotland, along with 96.3% of its 6,095 private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across IV postcodes, the Volkswagen Caddy was in the top three diesel vans. For a loaded Caddy or a bigger van, Stage 1 is about torque, kept within the clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Ellesmere Port
intro: The M53 and the M56 both appear among Ellesmere Port's main roads, alongside the A41, A5117, A550 and A494. For a diesel that mixes motorway miles with fast A roads, Stage 1 remapping makes the most sense. The change is made to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within its limits, so nothing is bolted on and the car looks the same. The gain shows as mid-range torque: pulling cleanly from a slip road into motorway traffic, or passing a slower vehicle on an A road, without dropping a gear. What it does change is how the engine delivers its power. The fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits, and on a diesel the gain you feel most is mid-range pull for overtaking and joining faster roads.
