name: Leeds
intro: There were 98,140 privately kept diesel cars in the Leeds council area at the end of June 2026, 30.3% of the 324,311 private cars there, even after a 4.8% fall over the year. If you own one of them and hope a remap will cut your fuel bills, keep expectations modest: any change in economy depends on how the car is driven. The real reason for Stage 1 remapping is drivability. More mid-range torque means easier overtaking, stronger joins onto fast roads and fewer downshifts on hills, and it comes from a remap file matched to the vehicle, not from new parts. Your insurer must be told.
driving: Vans are a large group in the Leeds council area: 21,030 are privately kept, 95.9% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across LS postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car, ahead of the Ford Focus and BMW 3 Series. In the 2021 Census, 38.4% of working residents in the Leeds built-up area drove to work, below the 45.1% for England and Wales, and 35.1% of households had no car. Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is about 7 km away, and Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62 about 15 km. For a working van, a remap adds torque under load, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Leicester
intro: Around 45,000 diesel cars are privately kept in the Leicester council area: 45,079 at the end of June 2026, or 35.4% of all private cars, the 8th highest diesel share among the 104 largest towns we cover. The count has barely shifted either, down 3% on a year earlier, one of the smallest falls in that group. For the drivers of those cars, the reason to consider a Stage 1 remap is mid-range torque: the pull that gets a car past slower traffic and up to speed on a slip road without dropping a gear. Any fuel saving depends on how the car is driven, so it is never something to count on.
driving: The M1 and M69 both feature among Leicester's main roads, along with the A6 and A47, and Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is 4.7 km away. Wigston is 5.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 44.9% of working residents in the Leicester built-up area drove to work and 30.8% of households had no car. In the council area, plug-ins are just 3.3% of private cars, one of the lowest shares of the 104, and 96.5% of the 5,848 private vans are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across LE postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. With a van, the remap is shaped around the gearbox and clutch as well as the engine.

name: Leigh
intro: Leigh's main road list consists of A roads. Its main routes are all A roads, among them the A580, A579, A577, A58, A6, A578, A572 and A574, and the nearest service area, Rivington on the M61, is 11.3 km away. On A-road driving, the part of Stage 1 remapping you notice is mid-range torque: firmer pull out of junctions, easier overtaking and fewer downshifts when the road climbs. The remap itself is software only, adjusting the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits. A diesel with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first, and your insurer needs to know once the work is done.
driving: Atherton and Golborne are each 4.2 km from Leigh, Hindley 4.6 km, Platt Bridge and Abram 4.7 km and Tyldesley 4.9 km. Even so, 22.8% of working residents in the Leigh built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, above the England and Wales figure of 19%, and 56.4% drove. A quarter of households, 25.6%, had no car or van, more than across the Wigan council area (21.3%). The council area had 78 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, close to England's 81. In 2025 MOT tests across WN postcodes, the Ford Transit and Transit Custom were the most tested diesel vans. Fully loaded, a remapped Transit Custom needs less work through the gears.

name: Leighton Buzzard
intro: Leighton Buzzard's working residents travelled further in the 2021 Census than those across the Central Bedfordshire council area: in the built-up area, 8.6% went 30 km or more to work, against 7.6% across the council area and 4.4% across England and Wales. That was on a lockdown census day, so normal commuting was higher. When a car covers that kind of distance, running costs matter, so it is worth being straight about Stage 1 remapping: any change in fuel economy depends on how you drive and is modest. The case for it is how the car drives. On a diesel, mid-range torque rises, so long runs need fewer downshifts and overtaking takes less effort.
driving: No motorway is among Leighton Buzzard's main roads, which include the A5 and A418, yet its three nearest service areas, from Toddington at 11.4 km to Newport Pagnell at 19 km, are all on the M1. Bletchley is 9.5 km away. Of households in the built-up area, 44% had two or more cars in the 2021 Census, against 35.4% across England and Wales. Privately kept diesel cars in the Central Bedfordshire council area fell 6.9% in the year to June 2026, against 5.3% across England. The Vauxhall Astra and BMW 5 Series were both among the five most tested diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across LU postcodes. On M1 runs in a 5 Series, easier overtaking is what you notice.

name: Letchworth
intro: Letchworth's nearest neighbour, Baldock, is just 2.7 km away, and ExtraMSA Baldock Services on the A1(M) is 4.2 km off, so the motorway is close at hand for longer trips. In the 2021 Census, 20.1% of households in the Letchworth built-up area had no car, more than the 15.5% across the North Hertfordshire council area, though below the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. A Stage 1 remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with no new parts. On a diesel the gain is mid-range torque, which shows when you join the A1(M) from the slip road or carry a load. It does not change the vehicle's emissions standard either.
driving: Six main roads are listed for Letchworth, among them the A1(M), A1 and A505. Stotfold is 4 km away and Stevenage 8.1 km. The town's street plan includes Sollershott Circus, built around 1909 and described as the United Kingdom's first roundabout. In the 2021 Census, 6.7% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 42.9% drove to work, against 45.1%. The North Hertfordshire council area had 65 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, under England's 81. The Nissan Qashqai was among the three most tested diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across SG postcodes; on a car like that, a remap mainly makes overtaking less hurried.

name: Lewisham
intro: Lewisham leans heavily towards petrol. At the end of June 2026, 72.3% of privately kept cars in the council area ran on it, and diesel made up just 12.2%, the 3rd lowest diesel share of the 104 largest towns we cover. So if you are looking at Stage 1 remapping in Lewisham, there is a good chance the car is a petrol. Petrol or diesel, the job is the same in principle: fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits. On the 8,555 diesel cars, down from 8,956 a year earlier, the change shows most as mid-range torque. On either fuel, insurers must be told about a remap.
driving: The A2, A20, A21 and A205 head Lewisham's main road list, which has no motorway, and RoadChef Clacket Lane Services on the M25, the nearest listed service area, is 20 km away. The whole borough falls within the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily, and a remap won't change a vehicle's emissions standard. In the 2021 Census, 15.9% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 47.7% of households had no car. The 3,010 private vans were 87.3% diesel at the end of June 2026, and in 2025 MOT tests across SE postcodes the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the diesel vans. Stage 1 suits a van that carries a load, within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Leyland
intro: Leyland's nearest service area is Charnock Richard on the M6, 7.1 km away, with Rivington on the M61 at 13.4 km and Blackburn with Darwen on the M65 at 14.8 km. With three motorways in that range, longer trips from the PR25 and PR26 districts are likely to include a motorway leg. For a diesel that spends time at motorway speed, Stage 1 remapping is mostly felt as extra mid-range torque: the car holds its pace on gradients, overtakes with less planning and needs fewer downshifts. All of it is done in software, by changing the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Economy changes are modest and depend on how the car is driven.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 18.2% of working residents in the Leyland built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work and 4.1% went 30 km or more, both a little above the South Ribble council area's 16.7% and 3.9%. Euxton is 3.4 km away, Bamber Bridge 4.4 km and Chorley 6.4 km. Privately kept diesel cars in the South Ribble council area fell by 6.8% in the year to June 2026, against 5.3% across England, yet 95.5% of privately kept vans there were still diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across PR postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf, Nissan Qashqai and BMW 3 Series were among the most tested diesel cars. On cars like these, a remap mainly brings easier overtaking and smoother joins onto the M6.

name: Lichfield
intro: Lichfield's road list mixes a toll motorway, the M6 Toll, with the A38 and a run of other A roads, including the A51, A461, A5206 and A5127. On whichever of those roads a car spends its time, Stage 1 remapping works the same way: a remap file matched to the vehicle adjusts fuel, boost and timing in software, within what the engine was designed to handle, and nothing you could see under the bonnet changes. A diesel comes away with stronger mid-range torque, felt most with a full load or a trailer behind. If a dashboard fault is showing, it is fixed before any remap.
driving: Lichfield is a cathedral city, and its nearest neighbour is Burntwood, 6.6 km away, with Rugeley at 11.7 km. The M6 Toll's Norton Canes services is the closest stop, 9.8 km off, and Tamworth Services on the M42 is 15.1 km. In the 2021 Census, 47.5% of working residents in the Lichfield built-up area drove to work, below the 54.9% for the council area, while 25.9% travelled 10 km or more, above the England and Wales figure of 19%. The Lichfield council area lost 7.5% of its privately kept diesel cars in the year to June 2026, against a 5.3% fall across England. In 2025 MOT tests across WS postcodes, the Ford Transit Custom was fifth among diesel vans; loaded, it gains low-rev pull from a remap.

name: Lincoln
intro: Across LN postcodes, 46.2% of the cars and small vans given an MOT in 2025 were diesel. The council figures point the same way: at the end of June 2026, 35.2% of privately kept cars in the Lincoln council area ran on diesel, the 10th highest share of the 104 largest towns we cover. For diesel owners, Stage 1 remapping changes the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. In practice that means mid-range torque: overtaking on A roads with less waiting for a gap, and fewer downshifts with a load. Insurers must be told about a remap, and any fault is repaired first.
driving: No motorway appears among Lincoln's main roads. The A46, A15, A57 and A607 do that job, with the A1192 and A1434, and Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46 is 5.2 km out. North Hykeham is just 2.9 km away, but Newark-on-Trent is 21.4 km and Sleaford 25.8 km. In the 2021 Census, 5.9% of working residents in the Lincoln built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. Plug-in cars are rare: 3.6% of private cars in the council area, one of the lowest shares of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across LN postcodes, the Ford Transit and Vauxhall Vivaro were the most tested diesel vans. Longer A-road trips are where a remap's extra torque is most useful.

name: Lisburn

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021, during a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual. NISRA settlement figures are approximated from small areas; workers exclude full-time students, and distance bands count work within Northern Ireland only.

intro: With the M1 on its road list and Lisburn Services just 2.1 km away, Lisburn puts motorway driving close at hand. If you tow on the M1, or regularly carry a full load, Stage 1 remapping is felt where a diesel works hardest: the extra mid-range torque makes a trailer feel lighter and means the engine holds its gear when traffic speeds up, instead of needing a downshift. It is a software change only, to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits. Fuel use may change a little depending on how you drive, but no saving is promised, and your insurer has to be told.
driving: Lisburn stands on the River Lagan, and the A1, A3, A30 and A49 are among its other main roads. Belfast is 10.8 km away and Castlereagh 11.2 km, and beyond Lisburn Services the next stop, Temple Patrick on the M2, is 19.1 km off. In the 2021 Census, 27.5% of working residents in the Lisburn City settlement travelled 10 km or more to work within Northern Ireland, above the 25.6% for Northern Ireland. In the Lisburn and Castlereagh council area, privately kept diesel cars fell from 33,173 to 31,748 in the year to June 2026, and there were 62 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, against 98 across Northern Ireland. For a car doing that commute daily, the extra torque mostly means less work for the driver.

name: Little Hulton
intro: Journeys to work from Little Hulton ran longer than across Salford as a whole in the 2021 Census. In the Little Hulton built-up area, 22.2% of working residents travelled 10 km or more, against 14.5% across the Salford council area and 19% across England and Wales. Those figures come from a census day in lockdown, when fewer people were commuting. Covering that kind of distance regularly is one of the stronger reasons to consider Stage 1 remapping on a diesel. The change is made in the engine's software, to its fuel, boost and timing settings, and stays within the engine's limits. In practice that means steadier pulling at speed and fewer downshifts when traffic bunches up.
driving: Four motorways appear on Little Hulton's road list, the M61, M60, M602 and M62, with the A6 and A580 among the A roads. The two nearest service areas, Rivington on the M61 and Moto Birch on the M62, are 13 km and 13.1 km away. Walkden is only 1.9 km off, Farnworth 2.4 km and Kearsley 3.2 km. In the 2021 Census, 51.1% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, well above the Salford council area's 41.1%. Among diesel vans given an MOT across M postcodes in 2025, the Volkswagen Transporter and Vauxhall Vivaro were among the most common. With a load in the back, a van like that gains low-rev pull from a remap, set within its gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Liverpool
intro: Two Fords head the list of diesel cars given an MOT across L postcodes in 2025: the Focus, with 5,527, and the Kuga, with 4,482. The Nissan Qashqai, BMW 3 Series and Volkswagen Golf follow. These are mostly everyday family cars, and that shapes what Stage 1 remapping means here: a stronger, more relaxed engine for daily driving rather than a performance project. Only the software changes, with fuel, boost and timing adjusted inside the engine's limits. On a diesel Focus or Kuga, the gain shows as mid-range torque: easier overtaking, smoother joins onto fast roads and fewer downshifts with a full car. Tell your insurer once it is done.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 39.5% of households in the Liverpool built-up area had no car, well above the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, and 40.4% of working residents drove to work. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is about 7 km away, and Old Meadow Services on the M58 about 12 km. Diesel is 29.5% of the council area's 154,751 private cars, down 5.4% in the year to June 2026. There are 9,071 privately kept vans, 96.8% of them diesel, and the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van across L postcodes in 2025, well ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. A loaded van gains torque from a remap, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Livingston
intro: Households with two or more cars are more common in the Livingston locality than in Scotland as a whole: 33.2% against 30.5% in Scotland's 2022 Census. The M8 is on the town's road list. On a diesel, Stage 1 remapping changes the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within its limits, and the result is more mid-range torque. You notice it joining the motorway, moving out to overtake and keeping pace on an incline without changing down. Nothing is bolted on. Fuel use may move a little either way depending on your driving, and your insurer needs to know about the remap.
driving: Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is 15.1 km from Livingston, and Dreghorn on the A720 is 18.2 km. The A71, A89 and A899 are among the town's A roads, and Linlithgow, Whitburn and Armadale are all a little over 10 km away. Plug-in cars made up 6.2% of the West Lothian council area's privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, a slightly bigger slice than Scotland's 5.1%. In 2025 MOT tests across EH postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, with the Volkswagen Transporter and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter next. A Sprinter with a load on feels a remap most as stronger mid-range pull on the M8 or the A71.

name: Llanelli
intro: There were 146 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars in the Carmarthenshire council area at the end of June 2026, well above the Wales figure of 117, and 96.3% of those vans ran on diesel. Across the county that adds up to a lot of working diesels, and for a van, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about pulling power when it is loaded or towing. The fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. The gearbox and clutch still set how far a van's remap should go, which is why the work starts from a remap file matched to the vehicle.
driving: The main roads listed around Llanelli are all A roads, the A4138, A484, A4214, A476 and A4240, but the M4 is close, with Pont Abraham Services 8.8 km away and Swansea West 10.2 km. Gorseinon is the nearest neighbour at 7.2 km, and Swansea is 15.4 km off. The 2021 Census found 63.1% of working residents of the Llanelli built-up area driving to work, far above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 29.5% travelling 10 km or more. Diesel accounted for 38.7% of privately kept cars in the Carmarthenshire council area in June 2026, above the 36.1% for Wales. On a car used for a daily run towards Swansea, Stage 1 mostly shows up as easier overtaking and fewer downshifts.

name: Locks Heath
intro: No service area is closer to Locks Heath than 16.2 km: that is Rownhams Services on the M27, with Farlington Services on the A27 at 16.7 km and West Wellow Services on the A36 at 21 km. Reaching any of them means a proper run, and steady driving of that kind is where Stage 1 remapping earns its place. The remap is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, with no hardware added. On a diesel, the extra mid-range torque makes overtaking on the A27 less of a stretch and means fewer downshifts on the way. Changes to fuel use, if any, are small and depend on how you drive.
driving: Villages surround Locks Heath, among them Sarisbury, Warsash and Titchfield. Fareham is 5.6 km away, Lee-on-the-Solent 6.1 km and Hedge End 6.8 km, and the A3051, A3025 and A3024 are among the roads on the list. Households here are well supplied with cars: in the 2021 Census, 54.1% of those in the Locks Heath built-up area had two or more, against 35.4% for England and Wales and 49.8% for the Fareham council area, and only 9.3% had none. The council area's privately kept cars were 25.9% diesel at the end of June 2026. The Mercedes-Benz Sprinter made the top five diesel vans in 2025 MOT tests across SO postcodes. For a family diesel towing or a loaded van, Stage 1 adds useful pull.

name: Long Eaton
intro: Long Eaton's main roads include the M1, the A50 and the A52, with the A453, A6005 and A6007 alongside them. With roads like these close by, the part of the rev range you use most is the middle, when you join, overtake and hold speed with traffic. On a diesel, Stage 1 remapping adds torque through that mid-range, so a car or van pulls without dropping a gear. The change is made to the fuel, boost and timing settings in software, kept within the engine's limits. Fuel economy may move a little either way depending on how you drive, so it is not a reason on its own to remap.
driving: Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 is the nearest stop, 6 km from Long Eaton, and two M1 service areas, Trowell and Moto Donington Park, are both about 8 km out. In the 2021 Census, 20.1% of working residents in the Long Eaton built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, slightly above 19% for England and Wales, and 21.1% of households had no car. The Erewash council area had 93 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 in England. In 2025 MOT tests across NG postcodes, the Volkswagen Transporter and Vauxhall Vivaro followed the Ford Transit as the most tested diesel vans. Remapped, vans like these pull a load more easily, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Longbenton
intro: Just 9.3% of working residents in the Longbenton built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, about half the England and Wales figure of 19% and below the 14.6% for the North Tyneside council area. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is the nearest service area, 6.2 km off. For a diesel that mostly does short local runs with the odd trip up the A1, a Stage 1 remap is judged on how the car pulls in the mid-range.

name: Loughborough
intro: Car ownership in Loughborough is noticeably lower than in the Charnwood council area around it. In the 2021 Census, 22.8% of households in the Loughborough built-up area had no car, against 15.6% across the council area, and 34.8% had two or more, compared with 43.9%. In a single-car household that one car covers every kind of trip, from short hops across town to longer motorway runs, so it helps if the engine copes well with both. Stage 1 remapping adjusts fuel, boost and timing in software, staying inside the engine's limits. On a diesel, expect stronger mid-range torque rather than any visible change, since nothing is bolted on.
driving: Moto Donington Park Services on the M1 is 8.2 km from Loughborough, and the A6 and A46 each have a service area within about 11 km. Shepshed is 4.6 km away, Mountsorrel 7.4 km and Coalville 10.7 km. MOT tests in 2025 across LE postcodes put the BMW 3 Series third among diesel cars. On a 3 Series, a remap mainly sharpens the response when you need to pass slower traffic on the A6.

name: Loughton
intro: For a town with the M11 and M25 among its main roads, Loughton had remarkably few long commutes in the 2021 Census: just 1.7% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, under the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. Middle distances were another matter, with 21.2% going 10 km or more, above the 19% for England and Wales. That points to plenty of medium-length runs rather than long hauls. On those, Stage 1 remapping is about response: a diesel gains mid-range torque, so joining the M25 or passing on the A121 takes less effort. No parts are fitted. The remap works on the fuel, boost and timing settings, within what the engine is built to handle.
driving: Loughton sits just outside Greater London. Buckhurst Hill and Chigwell are both within 4 km, and Epping is 5.3 km away. The nearest listed service area, South Mimms on the A1(M), is 20.9 km off. In the 2021 Census, 34.9% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, under the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Petrol is the main fuel in the Epping Forest council area: 65% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, with diesel at 19.1% against 29.1% in England. MOT tests in 2025 across IG postcodes put the Mercedes-Benz E Class and BMW 5 Series at the top of the diesel car list. On cars like these, a remap is felt as stronger pull from low revs.

name: Lowestoft
intro: In the Lowestoft built-up area, 10.6% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and census day fell during a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual. Long journeys like that are where a diesel's character matters, and Stage 1 remapping works on exactly that: stronger torque in the mid-range, so the engine responds more readily when accelerating on an A-road. Only the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings change, in software and within its limits. How it affects fuel use depends on the way you drive, and any change is modest.
driving: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest listed service area to Lowestoft, 36.8 km away. Gorleston-on-Sea, at 10.8 km, is the closest place, with Great Yarmouth at 14.2 km and Norwich about 35 km off. The A12 and A47 head the road list, with the A146 next. In the 2021 Census, 57.7% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Loaded vans covering those distances gain most from a remap's extra pull at low revs.

name: Luton
intro: Commercial vehicle manufacturing in Luton came to an end in 2025, but vans still matter here. The Luton council area had 4,554 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 96.7% of them diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across LU postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. If yours is a van that spends the day loaded, the first thing you would notice after a Stage 1 remap is how it pulls from low revs, with fewer gear changes. On longer runs, mid-range torque is what you notice.

name: Lytham St Anne's
intro: None of the service areas listed for Lytham St Anne's is closer than 24.2 km. The nearest is Charnock Richard on the M6, with Old Meadow on the M58 at 27 km and Lancaster Services at 28.2 km. In the Fylde council area, diesel made up 29% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, almost level with England's 29.1%. Among diesel cars, the BMW 3 Series was the most tested in 2025 MOT tests across FY postcodes. name: Macclesfield
intro: Macclesfield relies on A-roads: the A537, A523, A536 and A538 make up its main road list, and the nearest motorway service area, Knutsford Services on the M6, is 18.4 km away. For a car that covers most of its miles on roads like these, Stage 1 remapping is about overtaking slower traffic and pulling cleanly out of bends and junctions. Only the software changes: the fuel, boost and timing settings are revised within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. On a diesel, the mid-range torque gain means fewer downshifts. name: Newport
intro: Nearly half the cars and small vans given an MOT across NP postcodes in 2025 were diesel: 45.9%. That covers the whole postcode area rather than Newport alone, but the council figures point the same way, with 33.1% of the 77,340 privately kept cars in the Newport council area running on diesel at the end of June 2026. For all those diesel owners, a Stage 1 remap is about the mid-range. The result you feel is torque at everyday revs, the kind that helps with a full boot, a trailer or a long climb, all from a change to the engine's software rather than its hardware.
driving: The M4 and A48(M) are both among Newport's main roads, and the three nearest listed service areas are all on the M4, the closest being Cardiff Gate at 10 km and Magor at 11.5 km. Cwmbrân is 7.6 km away and Cardiff 15.8 km. In the 2021 Census, 52.2% of working residents in the Newport built-up area drove to work and 20.5% travelled 10 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 19%. The council area has 5,773 private vans, 75 for every 1,000 private cars, and 95.9% are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NP postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car. Gearbox and clutch limits matter on any van remap.

name: Newport
intro: The Isle of Wight council area had 10,493 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, which works out at 148 for every 1,000 private cars, against 81 across England. Newport is the island's county town. Vans carry loads and tow, so the part of Stage 1 remapping that matters for them is torque low and in the middle of the rev range rather than speed. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Insurers must be told about a remap, for a van as much as for a car.
driving: Newport's main roads are the A3020, A3054, A3056 and A3021. Cowes is 5.6 km away, Ryde 10 km and Sandown 10.5 km. Few journeys to work were long in the 2021 Census: 12.2% of working residents in the Newport built-up area travelled 10 km or more and only 2% went 30 km or more, both below the England and Wales figures of 19% and 4.4%. Even so, 50.2% drove to work, against 45.1%. Diesel cars are holding on across the Isle of Wight council area, where their number fell just 1.6% over the year to June 2026, against 5.3% for England. On short, regular A-road trips, a remap is felt as quicker response from low revs rather than extra top speed.

name: Newry

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021, during a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual. NISRA settlement figures are approximated from small areas; workers exclude full-time students, and distance bands count work within Northern Ireland only.

intro: Diesel still accounts for 61.4% of privately kept cars in the Newry, Mourne and Down council area, against 52.7% across Northern Ireland, according to figures for the end of June 2026. The same council area had 12,332 private vans, 98.3% of them diesel. With that many diesels on the road, Stage 1 remapping is a fair question to ask before you think about changing vehicle. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, and nothing is added to the engine. The difference most diesel drivers feel is stronger mid-range pull, which helps when overtaking, joining faster traffic or carrying weight.
driving: The A1 is on the Newry road list, with the A2, A25, A27 and A28, and the town sits on the way between Belfast and Dublin. Motorway stops are some distance off: Cohannon Services on the M1 is 41.5 km away and Lisburn Services 44.3 km. Of the neighbouring towns listed, Banbridge is 19.4 km away and Armagh 28.7 km. In the 2021 Census, taken during a lockdown, 14% of working residents in the Newry settlement travelled 10 km or more, below the Northern Ireland figure of 25.6%, and 23.1% of households had no car, above the 19.5% for Northern Ireland. For vans, extra torque matters most on loaded runs, with the gearbox and clutch kept within their limits.

name: Newton Aycliffe
intro: Forest Park Services is just 4 km from Newton Aycliffe on the A1(M), and Bradbury Services on the same motorway is 5.7 km away. With the motorway that close, plenty of journeys from DL5 begin on a slip road, which is a good test of a diesel's mid-range. Stage 1 remapping alters the fuel, boost and timing settings, keeps inside the engine's limits and adds nothing to the engine bay. You notice the extra torque when merging at speed and when overtaking, and a loaded van needs fewer gear changes to keep up with traffic. A vehicle with a DPF, EGR or injector fault has that repaired before any remap.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 58.8% of working residents in the Newton Aycliffe built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 25.9% of households had no car. Away from the motorway, the A167, A689, A68 and A6072 are listed, and Sedgefield Services on the A689 is 9.5 km off. Bishop Auckland is 8 km away and Darlington 10.3 km. The number of privately kept diesel cars in the County Durham council area fell 5.7% in the year to June 2026, a little faster than England's 5.3%. MOT tests at DL postcode test stations in 2025 had the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter as the two most tested diesel vans. Those vans show the benefit of a Stage 1 remap most when towing or fully loaded.

name: Newton Mearns
intro: Compared with Scotland as a whole, the East Renfrewshire council area had more petrol hybrids and plug-in cars at the end of June 2026: 10.7% and 7.4% of privately kept cars, against 8.5% and 5.1%. Diesel was down to 22.3%. For the diesel and petrol cars in that mix, Stage 1 remapping is still relevant. The remap changes fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits, and leaves the hardware as it is. On a diesel SUV or estate, the gain you notice is mid-range torque when overtaking or climbing, with fewer downshifts. Fuel use changes are modest and depend on how you drive.
driving: Main roads listed for Newton Mearns include the M77 and A77, and the A726, A727 and A736 complete the list. RoadChef Bothwell Services at 17.3 km and RoadChef Hamilton Services at 18.5 km are the nearest service areas, both on the M74. In Scotland's 2022 Census, 51.2% of households in the locality had two or more cars, against 30.5% across Scotland, and commuting reached further than the Scotland figure: 28.3% of working residents travelled 10 km or more, compared with 20.4%. Giffnock lies 3.7 km away and Barrhead 4.6 km, with Paisley at 9.2 km. In 2025 MOT tests across G postcodes, the BMW 3 Series was among the five most tested diesel cars, a car where extra mid-range torque makes motorway overtakes easier.

name: Newtownabbey

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021, during a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual. NISRA settlement figures are approximated from small areas; workers exclude full-time students, and distance bands count work within Northern Ireland only.

intro: Three motorways and the A8(M) serve Newtownabbey: the M2, M3 and M5 all appear among its main roads, along with the A2, A6, A8 and A55, and Belfast is only 7.1 km away. For drivers who use those roads, Stage 1 remapping helps most when joining and overtaking: the extra mid-range torque on a diesel means less need to change down and a firmer pull up to speed. The remap alters only the fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine's software, staying within its limits. A vehicle with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired first, and once the work is done your insurer has to be told.
driving: Newtownabbey wraps around Carnmoney Hill, with Holywood 5.9 km away, Carrickfergus 9.1 km, Castlereagh 9.7 km and Ballyclare 11.7 km. The closest service area is Temple Patrick on the M2, northbound, 8 km out, and Lisburn Services on the M1 is 16.1 km. In the 2021 Census, 21.6% of working residents in the Metropolitan Newtownabbey settlement travelled 10 km or more to work within Northern Ireland, below the 25.6% for Northern Ireland as a whole, and 61.4% drove. Privately kept diesel cars in the Antrim and Newtownabbey council area fell from 34,716 to 33,593 in the year to June 2026. On shorter trips, the benefit is mostly in town traffic, where the engine pulls harder before it needs a gear change.

name: Newtownards

census.note: Collected on 21 March 2021, during a lockdown, so commuting was lower than usual. NISRA settlement figures are approximated from small areas; workers exclude full-time students, and distance bands count work within Northern Ireland only.

intro: At the northern tip of Strangford Lough, Newtownards has Bangor 7.8 km away, Holywood 10 km, Castlereagh 12.7 km and Belfast 15.1 km. Journeys of that length are long enough to notice what Stage 1 remapping does on a diesel: it pulls more firmly from low revs, gets up to speed with fewer gear changes and overtakes with less effort. Nothing is bolted on. The remap is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, and it stays within the engine's limits. A car with a DPF, AdBlue, EGR or injector fault is repaired before it is remapped, so the change goes onto a healthy engine.
driving: Lisburn Services on the M1, 21.5 km away, is the nearest service area to Newtownards, with Temple Patrick on the M2 at 23.9 km, and the town's main roads are the A2, A20, A21, A22, A48 and A221. In the 2021 Census, 63.7% of working residents in the Newtownards settlement drove to work and 26.6% travelled 10 km or more within Northern Ireland, both just above the Northern Ireland figures of 62.7% and 25.6%. In the Ards and North Down council area, privately kept diesel cars fell from 33,710 to 32,116 in the year to June 2026, and there were 67 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars, against 98 across Northern Ireland. On a regular commute, a remapped diesel picks up speed more readily, without a downshift.

name: Northampton
intro: Diesel still made up 42.4% of the cars and small vans given an MOT at test stations across NN postcodes in 2025, and the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, with 6,211. In the West Northamptonshire council area, 33.3% of the 227,114 privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026. That is a lot of diesel engines, and on a diesel the gain from Stage 1 remapping is mid-range torque: easier overtaking, joining the M1 with less effort, and steadier pulling with a trailer. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on.
driving: Northampton Services on the M1 is 4.6 km away, and Red Lion Truckstop, also on the M1, is 7.5 km. The A43, A45, A428 and A508 are on the main road list too. In the 2021 Census, 50.3% of working residents in the Northampton built-up area drove to work, above 45.1% for England and Wales, and 4.9% travelled 30 km or more. The council area had 17,487 privately kept vans in June 2026, 77 for every 1,000 cars and 94.3% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NN postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, followed by the Volkswagen Transporter. For a van running loaded on the M1, Stage 1 torque helps, provided the clutch and gearbox are in good health.

name: Northfleet
intro: Northfleet sits in a tight cluster of places. Swanscombe is 2.8 km away in a straight line, Tilbury 3.1 km and Gravesend 3.2 km, with Grays at 5.1 km and Chadwell St Mary at 5.4 km. Neighbours that close mean a lot of short trips, with longer runs mixed in when work or family takes you further. Stage 1 remapping suits that mix, because what it adds on a diesel is pull low in the rev range rather than extra top speed. You feel it pulling away from a junction, filtering onto a main road from a slip road, or climbing with a car full of shopping. Nothing is bolted on, and the engine's own limits are kept to.
driving: Just over half of working residents in the Northfleet built-up area, 50.3%, drove to work in the 2021 Census, against 45.1% across England and Wales. Fewer households had two or more cars, though: 32.9%, against 35.4%. The A2, A1089, A226 and A2260 are among the main roads, and Tollgate Services on the A2 is 2.8 km away, with Moto Thurrock on the M25 at 7.6 km. Privately kept vans in the Gravesham council area came to 64 per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, under England's 81. In 2025 MOT tests across DA postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Transit Custom. A loaded Transit gains more low-rev pull from Stage 1, within its clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Norwich
intro: Petrol and diesel still power almost every private car in Norwich. Plug-ins are just 2.9% of privately kept cars in the Norwich council area, the second lowest share of the 104 largest towns we cover, while 58.4% run on petrol and 32.8% on diesel. Those engines are what Stage 1 remapping works on. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the benefit you feel is mid-range torque, which takes the effort out of overtaking and pulling with a load. Changes in fuel use are modest and depend on how you drive.
driving: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is 6 km from Norwich, but the next nearest service areas are 56.6 km and 61.6 km away. The A11, A47 and A140 are among the main roads. Taverham and Drayton is 6.6 km away, Wymondham 13.7 km and Dereham 23.1 km. In the 2021 Census, 42.4% of working residents in the Norwich built-up area drove to work. Privately kept diesel cars in the council area fell only 3.3% over the year to June 2026, one of the smallest falls of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across NR postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans. On long A-road runs, a remap's mid-range torque makes overtaking easier.

name: Nottingham
intro: Trent Bridge Services, on the A6011, is under 4 km from Nottingham, and two more service areas lie within 8 km: Trowell on the M1 and Pierrepont on the A52. Diesel is common here: 34.1% of privately kept cars in the Nottingham council area run on it, the 13th highest share of the 104 largest towns we cover. On a diesel, Stage 1 remapping is felt as mid-range torque, which shows when joining the M1 from a slip road, passing a slow lorry on the A52 or climbing without changing down. Your insurer must be told, and a car with a fault is repaired before any remap.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 38.3% of working residents in the Nottingham built-up area drove to work, and the same share of households, 38.3%, had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales. Arnold, West Bridgford and Beeston are all within about 6 km. The council area has 6,283 privately kept vans, 95.8% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NG postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van by a long way, at 11,282, with the Volkswagen Transporter and Vauxhall Vivaro next, while the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus led the diesel cars. For a van, a remap adds torque for loads and towing, within the limits of the gearbox and clutch.

name: Nuneaton
intro: Multiple-car households made up 40% of the total in the Nuneaton built-up area in the 2021 Census, above the 35.4% for England and Wales. Commuting distances were longer than average, too: 24.7% of working residents travelled 10 km or more to work, more than the 19% across England and Wales and the 23% for the Nuneaton and Bedworth council area, and that was on a census day in lockdown. More cars and longer trips make Stage 1 remapping worth a look. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, and on a diesel it brings stronger mid-range torque, so the car holds its pace on inclines and overtakes with less effort.
driving: Hinckley is only 5.7 km from Nuneaton and Bedworth 6.1 km, while the M69, A5 and A47 head further afield. For a motorway stop, Corley Services on the M6 is 8.5 km away and Tamworth Services on the M42 15.4 km. In 2025 MOT tests across CV postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter. The Nuneaton and Bedworth council area had 75 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, a little below the England figure of 81. For a loaded Transit or a car towing on the A5, the useful part of Stage 1 is extra pull at low revs, set within what the clutch and gearbox can handle.

name: Oldbury
intro: Rowley Regis is 2.1 km from Oldbury, Smethwick 3 km and West Bromwich 4.1 km, with Cradley Heath at 4.3 km and Dudley at 5.2 km. Commutes from the town were mostly short in the 2021 Census: only 12.8% of working residents in the Oldbury built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales. For a diesel that mostly does short urban work, Stage 1 remapping is less about speed and more about how the car behaves in traffic. The software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, gives more torque low in the rev range, so pulling away and slotting into gaps feels easier. No parts are added to the engine.
driving: Oldbury is the administrative centre of Sandwell. The M5 heads the town's list of main roads, with the A4123, A456 and A4031, and Moto Frankley Services on the M5 is 7.5 km away. Driving was how 53.4% of working residents in the Oldbury built-up area got to work in the 2021 Census, compared with 45.1% across England and Wales, while 26.7% of households had no car. In the Sandwell council area, 33.6% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% for England. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz C Class was among the most tested diesel cars. On the M5, a C Class or similar diesel with a Stage 1 remap overtakes with less effort, thanks to stronger mid-range pull.

name: Oldham
intro: High ground shapes driving in Oldham, which stands on elevated land among the Pennines. Hills are where a diesel shows what its mid-range is worth, and that is the part of the rev range a Stage 1 remap works on. Nothing is added to the engine; only its settings change, within its limits. The result is more pull from lower revs, so a car or loaded van holds its gear on a climb instead of changing down. At the end of June 2026, 30.4% of the 95,903 privately kept cars in the Oldham council area were diesel, along with 96.5% of its 6,232 private vans.
driving: Neighbouring towns are packed close: Lees is 2.6 km away, Royton 3.4 km and Chadderton 3.6 km. The M60 and A627(M) are among Oldham's main roads, with the A62 and A663, and the nearest listed service area is Moto Birch on the M62, 9.1 km away. In the 2021 Census, 50.7% of working residents in the Oldham built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 35% of households had no car. Private diesel cars in the council area fell from 30,944 to 29,196 over the year. In 2025 MOT tests across OL postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars, with the Audi A3 in the top five, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the vans.

name: Ormskirk
intro: Almost a third of Ormskirk's working residents travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census: 31.6% in the built-up area, against 19% across England and Wales and 26.3% across the West Lancashire council area. Another measure points the same way, with 5.8% going 30 km or more, against 4.4% across England and Wales. Both figures were taken in a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual. Runs of that length are where a diesel with a Stage 1 remap feels most settled: more mid-range torque means the car holds its speed, overtakes with less effort and needs fewer downshifts. The remap works through the engine's control unit, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits, so no parts are added.
driving: Maghull and Skelmersdale are both 6.7 km from Ormskirk, and Southport is 10.9 km away. The M58 is the only motorway on the town's road list, alongside the A570, A59 and A577, and Old Meadow Services on it is 5.6 km off. In the 2021 Census, 42.2% of households in the Ormskirk built-up area had two or more cars, against 35.4% across England and Wales. In the West Lancashire council area, there were 87 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, above England's 81. The Ford Transit topped the diesel vans in 2025 MOT tests across L postcodes, and a Transit that tows or runs heavy gains from more torque low down, provided the clutch and gearbox are up to it.

name: Oxford

caz.name: Oxford Zero Emission Zone
caz.scope: It is a pilot covering a few city-centre streets and charges any vehicle that is not zero emission.

intro: A pilot Zero Emission Zone on streets in Oxford city centre, including New Road, Bonn Square, Ship Street and St Michael's Street, charges a daily fee to any car or van that is not zero emission. Away from those streets, Stage 1 remapping is about how the engine drives: a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within its limits, that gives a diesel more mid-range torque on the A34 and A40. Your insurer needs to know about it. What a remap can't do is change a vehicle's emissions standard, so a petrol or diesel car is charged in the pilot zone with or without one.
driving: Peartree Services on the A44 is 4.6 km away and Welcome Break Oxford Services on the M40 is 11.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 23.8% of working residents in the Oxford built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% for England and Wales, and 31.2% of households had no car. Diesel made up 29.1% of the 46,383 privately kept cars in the council area at the end of June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across OX postcodes, 40% of cars and small vans tested were diesel; the Volkswagen Golf and Land Rover Discovery were the top two diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter the top vans. For a Discovery that tows, Stage 1 torque is the useful part.

name: Paisley
intro: Renfrewshire, the council area that includes Paisley, had 20,090 privately kept diesel cars at the end of June 2026, down from 22,590 a year earlier. That 11.1% fall is steeper than the 9.2% drop across Scotland, and diesel is now 24.2% of the area's private cars, below the Scottish 27.7%. For a diesel that is staying on the road, Stage 1 remapping can make it feel stronger without any new parts. The change is made in software, to the fuel, boost and timing settings, and stays within what the engine can handle. Once the remap is on, it has to be declared to your insurer.
driving: In Scotland's 2022 Census, 34.7% of households in the Paisley locality had no car, above the 26.4% across Scotland, and only 2.4% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.9%. Paisley's road list takes in two motorways, the M77 and M8, as well as A roads such as the A737 and A726. Erskine and Clydebank, 7.2 km and 8 km away, are on the list of nearby places. The nearest listed service area, RoadChef Bothwell on the M74, is 23 km away. MOT tests at stations in the PA postcode area in 2025 put the Volkswagen Golf top of the diesel cars and the Ford Transit top of the diesel vans. On either, the extra mid-range is easiest to feel joining the M8.

name: Penarth
intro: Only 40.3% of working residents in the Penarth built-up area drove to work in the 2021 Census, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and just 10.4% travelled 10 km or more, a little over half the 19% across England and Wales. With Cardiff 6.4 km away, the commute here was often a short one, so a car's harder work tends to come elsewhere: the motorway trip, the holiday run or towing. Those are the jobs where a diesel with Stage 1 remapping feels different. Nothing physical changes: fuel, boost and timing are adjusted in the engine software, within its limits, and the result is more mid-range torque, so merging, overtaking and pulling a trailer all take less effort.
driving: Vans are scarcer in the Vale of Glamorgan than across Wales: the council area had 85 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 117 for Wales. In the Penarth built-up area, only 17.7% of households had no car at the 2021 Census, against 23.3% for England and Wales. The town sits at the southern end of Cardiff Bay, with the A48, A4232 and A470 among eight main roads listed around it, and the M4 services at Cardiff West and Cardiff Gate are 11.2 km and 11.4 km away. Diesel made up 42.3% of the cars and small vans given an MOT at CF postcode test stations in 2025. Heading out on the M4, a remapped diesel joins and overtakes with less effort.

name: Perth
intro: Perth and Kinross had 104 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars in the council area at the end of June 2026, well above the 84 across Scotland. Diesel is also more common across the council area, at 31.4% of private cars against 27.7% for Scotland, and 94.6% of its private vans run on it. For a working diesel van or pickup, Stage 1 remapping is mainly about mid-range torque. The remap is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside its limits, with nothing bolted on. With a trailer behind or a load in the back, that means fewer downshifts on a climb.
driving: Service areas around Perth are spread out: Moto Kinross Services is 21 km away on the M90, Balhaldie Services 34.4 km on the A9 and Forfar Services 41.9 km on the A90. In Scotland's 2022 Census, 6.4% of working residents in the Perth locality travelled 30 km or more to work, above the 4.9% across Scotland, while 30.9% of households had no car, against 26.4%. In 2025 MOT tests across PH postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, followed by the Volkswagen Transporter, Ford Ranger and Toyota Hilux. On an A9 run with a trailer behind, steady mid-range pull matters more than outright speed.

name: Peterborough
intro: No large town we cover has a higher diesel share than Peterborough. At the end of June 2026, 40.3% of privately kept cars in the Peterborough council area were diesel, the highest of the 104 largest towns we cover, with petrol at 47.7%. That is 38,732 diesel cars. What Stage 1 remapping offers is aimed squarely at engines like these: more mid-range torque, which makes overtaking and joining the A1(M) easier and cuts down on downshifts. It is done in software, changing the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on.
driving: The A1 and A1(M) are both among Peterborough's main roads, with the A15, A16, A47 and A605. Kate's Cabin on the A1 is 5.7 km away, Peterborough Services on the A1(M) 6.1 km and the Stibbington Diner lorry park 9.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 5.7% of working residents in the Peterborough built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 48.1% drove. In 2025 MOT tests across PE postcodes, 47.7% of the cars and small vans tested were diesel, and the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Vauxhall Vivaro. On long A1 runs and with loaded vans, a remap's torque is the part you feel.

name: Pontefract
intro: On Pontefract's list of main roads, the M62 and the A1(M) sit alongside the A1, the A645 and the A639. For van drivers and anyone towing, routes like these mean long stretches at a steady speed with weight on board, and that is where Stage 1 remapping is most useful. Nothing is bolted on: the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within its limits. On a loaded van, extra mid-range torque means fewer downshifts and less labouring on gradients, though the gearbox and clutch set how far a van's remap should go. Fuel use afterwards depends on how the van is driven.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 36.3% of households in the Pontefract built-up area had two or more cars, a little above the 35.4% for both the Wakefield council area and England and Wales. Services are close: Moto Ferrybridge on the M62 is 2.9 km from the town in a straight line, Exelby Services Whitwood 6.4 km and Barnsdale Bar on the A1 8.7 km. Featherstone is 3.6 km away, Castleford 3.8 km and Normanton 6.9 km. The council area had 83 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81 in England, and in 2025 MOT tests across WF postcodes, 45.3% of the cars and small vans tested were diesel. On those diesels, a remap is felt as stronger pull from low revs.

name: Pontypool
intro: Monmouth Services on the A40 is the closest stop to Pontypool at 17.2 km, with Magor on the M4 at 17.4 km and Cardiff Gate at 18.4 km. So the nearest break is a similar distance away on either road, and the town's own main roads, the A4042, A472, A4043 and A4051, are all A roads. Over those distances a diesel with Stage 1 remapping feels different: more torque in the middle of the rev range, so it gets up to speed cleanly and needs fewer downshifts. Nothing is added to the engine: its fuel, boost and timing settings are altered in software and kept inside the limits it was built with.
driving: Driving to work was the norm in Pontypool at the 2021 Census: 64% of working residents in the built-up area drove, above both the England and Wales figure of 45.1% and the Torfaen council area's 61.9%. Households were well supplied with cars, too, as 40.1% had two or more, against 35.4% across England and Wales. Cwmbrân is 4.7 km away, Abertillery 9.2 km and Newport 12.2 km. In 2025 MOT tests across NP postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter made the top five diesel vans, and a loaded Sprinter gets more pulling power from Stage 1.

name: Pontypridd
intro: Pontypridd's list of main roads runs to eight, from the A470 and A4054 to the A472, and not one of them is a motorway. The closest motorway services, Cardiff West on the M4, are 10.9 km away, so reaching the motorway takes a stretch of A road first, with junctions and slower traffic to pass. For a diesel, that is where Stage 1 remapping shows: more torque in the mid-range means a cleaner overtake when a gap opens and fewer downshifts when the road rises.
