That second figure sits close to the England and Wales level of 35.4%. With more residents commuting by car, Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is worth a look for the daily run to work. The engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within its limits, and the result is stronger torque in the middle of the rev range, so the car pulls cleanly in a higher gear when traffic queues and moves off again.
driving: The town's nearest neighbours are Oldbury at 2.1 km and Cradley Heath at 2.6 km, with Dudley and Halesowen also under 5 km away. Only 14.7% of working residents travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census, below the 19% for England and Wales. The M5 is on the road list with the A4123, A461 and A4036, and Moto Frankley Services is 7.2 km away. Among diesel cars, the Nissan Qashqai and Ford Focus made the top five in 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes. In the Sandwell council area, 96.8% of privately kept vans were diesel at the end of June 2026. For a family Qashqai on short hops or a van on local jobs, Stage 1 makes pulling away with a full load easier.

name: Royal Leamington Spa
intro: Car commuting was less common in Royal Leamington Spa than across England and Wales in the 2021 Census: 35.1% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, against 45.1%, and the Warwick council area figure was 39.4%. Commutes were short as well, with only 15.2% travelling 10 km or more, and census day fell during a lockdown. A car that covers fewer commuting miles still has to handle town traffic and the occasional long trip, and Stage 1 remapping is about how the engine feels on all of them. The work itself is a software adjustment, with fuel, boost and timing recalibrated inside the engine's limits. On a diesel that does a lot of short runs, any DPF or EGR fault is repaired before the remap goes on.
driving: Leamington's nearest neighbour is Warwick, 3.7 km away, with Kenilworth at 6.5 km and Coventry at 13 km. The A452, A425 and A445 are among the town's main roads, and the nearest motorway services, on the M40, are 8.5 km off. Diesel is less common in the Warwick council area than in England as a whole: 25.8% of privately kept cars there were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% across England, while 6.7% were plug-ins. In 2025 MOT tests across CV postcodes, the BMW 1 Series made the top five diesel cars. On a 1 Series or a similar diesel hatchback used for town driving and the odd M40 run, Stage 1 gives a stronger mid-range for overtaking and a smoother pull from low revs.

name: Royal Sutton Coldfield
intro: Close to half of households in the Royal Sutton Coldfield built-up area had two or more cars in the 2021 Census: 45.9%, against 26.7% across the Birmingham council area and 35.4% for England and Wales. Only 15.3% had no car, less than half the council area's 31.7%. Where one of those cars is a diesel doing the longer trips, it is the natural one to consider for Stage 1 remapping. The change is made in software, to the fuel, boost and timing settings, and it stays inside the engine's limits. One practical point for homes with several cars: the insurer of the car being remapped must be told, even if the others stay as they are.
driving: The M6 Toll heads Royal Sutton Coldfield's list of main roads, with the A38, A453 and A452 among the rest. The nearest services are Tamworth on the M42, 13.4 km away, and RoadChef Norton Canes on the M6 Toll at 14.2 km. Streetly is 4.2 km from the town, Aldridge 7.6 km and Birmingham 10.1 km. In the 2021 Census, 21.3% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, above the 19% figure for England and Wales. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz C Class were among the most tested diesel cars. In either, a remap shows up as easier overtaking and a stronger pull up the slip road.

name: Royal Tunbridge Wells
intro: Vans are less common in the Tunbridge Wells council area than across England: at the end of June 2026 there were 73 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars, against 81. Petrol cars are in the majority, at 61.8% of privately kept cars, and diesel is under a quarter, at 23.5%. For diesel drivers in and around Royal Tunbridge Wells, Stage 1 remapping is a software change to fuel, boost and timing settings that stays within the engine's limits, with no parts fitted. The gain shows as mid-range torque, which makes overtaking easier and cuts the downshifts on hills. Your insurer needs to know about it.
driving: Tonbridge is the closest town to Royal Tunbridge Wells, 7 km away, while Crowborough is 11.5 km and East Grinstead 19.6 km. The A264 and A267 are among the main roads, alongside the A21 and A26. In the 2021 Census, 31.5% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars, below the 35.4% for England and Wales, and 33.5% of working residents drove to work, against 45.1%, though census day fell in a lockdown. Over the year to June 2026, the number of privately kept diesel cars in the Tunbridge Wells council area dropped 7.2%, more than England's 5.3%. For the diesels that remain, Stage 1 is felt most when overtaking on the A21 or A26, or when a full car needs to keep its pace.

name: Rugby
intro: Longer commutes show up in Rugby's census figures. In the 2021 Census, 5.4% of working residents in the Rugby built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, measured in a straight line, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and that was recorded during a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual. Stage 1 remapping is aimed at exactly that kind of distance driving. The remap is a change to the engine software, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits. On a diesel the result is stronger mid-range torque: steadier progress at motorway speed, cleaner overtakes and less need to change down when the road climbs. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive, and is modest either way.
driving: Three motorways appear on Rugby's road list, the M6, M45 and M1, alongside the A5, A45, A426 and A428. Rugby Services on the M6 is 3.8 km away and the Rugby Truck Stop on the A5 4 km, with Watford Gap on the M1 at 11.5 km. The Rugby council area had 19,754 privately kept diesel cars at the end of June 2026, 6.6% fewer than a year earlier and a bigger fall than England's 5.3%, yet diesel was still 31.5% of private cars. The BMW 3 Series came second only to the Volkswagen Golf among diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across CV postcodes. A 3 Series covering long M1 or M6 runs gains a stronger mid-range from Stage 1, useful for overtaking and for holding speed on gradients.

name: Rugeley
intro: One in three working residents in the Rugeley built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census: 33.2%, against 19% across England and Wales and 28.1% in the Cannock Chase council area. Census day fell during a lockdown, so this is not a picture of commuting today, but it marks Rugeley out as a place where a sizeable share of people had a longer journey to work. On longer drives, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about the mid-range: a diesel that pulls harder from low revs overtakes more easily and holds its speed on a climb without a downshift. Any change in fuel economy is modest and depends on how you drive.
driving: Rugeley's road list has no motorway on it: the A51, A513 and A460 are its main routes. The closest service area is RoadChef Norton Canes on the M6 Toll, 10.8 km away. Cannock is 8.3 km from the town, Lichfield 11.7 km and Stafford 11.9 km. In the 2021 Census, 5.6% of working residents travelled 30 km or more, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 61.7% drove to work. Across the Cannock Chase council area, 33.6% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, against 29.1% for England. In 2025 MOT tests across WS postcodes, the Nissan Qashqai and Ford Kuga were both in the top five diesel cars, and towing with either is where low-rev torque shows.

name: Runcorn
intro: Widnes is 5.6 km from Runcorn and Warrington 9.5 km, while Prescot, Northwich and St Helens all lie between 11.9 km and 13.6 km away. With that many towns in range, a car or van here may spend much of its week on short runs between them, with a motorway stretch for anything further. Stage 1 remapping suits that mix, because it improves the middle of the rev range rather than top speed. It is a software adjustment to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, and the vehicle looks exactly as it did. You notice it as stronger pulling from low revs, and your insurer needs to be told about it.
driving: Runcorn's road list has the M56 as its motorway, plus the A533, A557, A56, A5126, A562 and A558. Whitley Services on the A49 is the nearest at 7.5 km, with RoadChef Chester on the M56 and Burtonwood on the M62 both 10.3 km away. A quarter of households in the Runcorn built-up area, 25.4%, had no car at the 2021 Census, above 23.3% for England and Wales, while 53.1% of working residents drove to work, against 45.1%. The Ford Kuga topped the diesel cars tested at WA postcode MOT stations in 2025, just ahead of the Ford Focus. On an SUV like the Kuga, carrying a full load or a trailer, extra mid-range torque is the change you feel.

name: Rushden
intro: Two or more cars were available to 43.9% of households in the Rushden built-up area in the 2021 Census, against 35.4% across England and Wales, and just 14.9% had no car at all. When most homes have a car, and many have two, how those engines perform is a day-to-day matter. Stage 1 remapping is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, and the car looks exactly as it did. On a diesel the most noticeable change is extra torque through the middle of the rev range, so the car feels stronger with every seat taken or the boot full. Fuel use may shift slightly, depending on how you drive.
driving: Raunds and Wellingborough are Rushden's closest neighbours, at 7.2 km and 7.3 km, with Bedford 19.1 km away. The A6 and A45 are among the main roads, and Thrapston Services on the A45 is the nearest service area at 12.5 km. In the 2021 Census, 60.1% of working residents in the Rushden built-up area drove to work, above the North Northamptonshire council area's 57% and well above 45.1% for England and Wales. Across the council area, only 6% of privately kept cars were hybrid petrol at the end of June 2026, against 7.7% in England. For a diesel or petrol car on regular A6 and A45 runs, a remap is felt mainly as less effort when overtaking, and any vehicle with a fault is repaired first.

name: Rustington
intro: Only 14.7% of households in the Rustington built-up area had no car in the 2021 Census, fewer than the 16.9% for the Arun council area and well under the 23.3% across England and Wales, and 40.7% had two or more. Where one of those cars is a diesel, Stage 1 remapping adjusts fuel, boost and timing in the engine's software, within its limits. The gain is torque in the middle of the rev range, which is what you use pulling onto a faster road or passing a slow vehicle. Nothing is fitted, and fuel use changes, if at all, with how you drive. A vehicle with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired before the remap.
driving: The A280 and A284 are on Rustington's road list along with the A259 and A27, and Littlehampton is just 3.9 km off. Fontwell Services on the A27 is 12.6 km away and Buck Barn, on the A24, 21.5 km. The Arun council area's privately kept diesel cars went from 25,790 to 24,372 in the year to June 2026, a 5.5% drop, against 5.3% across England. In the 2021 Census, taken during a lockdown, 20.3% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% for England and Wales. Of the diesel cars given an MOT in BN postcodes in 2025, the Volkswagen Golf was tested most, ahead of the Nissan Qashqai. A diesel Golf or Qashqai with a remap picks up more readily when passing slower traffic on the A27.

name: Rutherglen
intro: Just 3.4 km separates Rutherglen from Cambuslang, and Glasgow is 5.6 km away, while the town's road list takes in four motorways, the M74 and M8 among them. Faster roads lean harder on an engine's mid-range than slow town streets do. Stage 1 remapping changes only software, so nothing is fitted, and on a diesel the extra pull sits in the mid-range, where motorway traffic asks for it. In practice that means fewer gear changes when you build speed or pull out to pass. The engine stays within its limits throughout. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive and is modest.
driving: RoadChef Bothwell Services is 9.2 km away on the M74, and RoadChef Hamilton Services 11.4 km. Homes without a car are common: 34.9% of households in the Rutherglen locality had no car in Scotland's 2022 Census, above the 26.4% across Scotland. A smaller share travelled 10 km or more to work, 12.5% of working residents against 20.4% for Scotland. Diesel made up 26% of privately kept cars in the South Lanarkshire council area at the end of June 2026, a little under Scotland's 27.7%. The Volkswagen Golf was the diesel car seen most often at MOT stations in G postcodes in 2025. On a diesel Golf, the extra mid-range shows when motorway traffic speeds up around you.

name: Sale
intro: Commuting by car was less common among working residents of Sale than across England and Wales in the 2021 Census. In the 2021 Census, 40.2% of working residents in the Sale built-up area drove, against 45.1% across England and Wales and 41.5% across the Trafford council area, on a census day that fell in a lockdown. If your car does more local trips than long commutes, Stage 1 remapping is less about cruising and more about response. Done in software alone, the remap adjusts the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings without going beyond its limits. On a diesel, the gain is mid-range torque, so the car pulls away more cleanly and needs fewer gear changes in traffic. Economy changes depend on how you drive and are modest.
driving: Diesel made up 26.2% of privately kept cars in the Trafford council area at the end of June 2026, below England's 29.1%. Stretford and Altrincham are the nearest towns to Sale, 3.3 km and 3.5 km away, with Wythenshawe at 4.3 km. The town's main roads include the M60 and M56 as well as the A56, A5181 and A6010, and the nearest service area is Tabley Hill on the M6, 13.9 km away. Addresses fall in the M33, M23, M32 and M21 postcode districts. In 2025 MOT tests across M postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz C Class and A Class were among the most tested diesel cars. A C Class or A Class diesel with a remap feels sharper in the mid-range, which helps when joining the M60.

name: Salford
intro: The M602, M60 and A57(M) are all on Salford's main road list, and Manchester city centre lies just across the River Irwell. On that mix of motorway-standard roads and city streets, the part of a diesel's performance that Stage 1 remapping changes is the mid-range. You get more torque for joining the M60, overtaking and pulling away loaded, with fewer downshifts. The remap is a software adjustment to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits. Fuel economy changes are modest and depend on how you drive, and any fault with the DPF, EGR or injectors is repaired before a remap.
driving: The closest listed service area is Moto Birch Services on the M62, 9.2 km away, and Old Trafford is 3.4 km off. In the 2021 Census, 44.3% of households in the Salford built-up area had no car, against 23.3% for England and Wales, and 30.6% of working residents drove to work. The Salford council area had 97,805 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 28.9% diesel and 57.9% petrol, and 5,889 private vans, 96.7% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across M postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter the vans. For a van that works across Greater Manchester, Stage 1 helps when loaded, within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Salisbury
intro: None of the three closest service areas to Salisbury is on a motorway. Rufus Stone on the A31 is 22.4 km away, West Wellow on the A36 is 22.7 km and Weyhill on the A303 is 24.1 km, so longer journeys from the city begin on A roads. That means overtaking and steady cruising, which is where Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is most useful. The remap alters the fuel, boost and timing settings in software and stays inside the engine's limits. Most drivers feel it as extra torque in the middle of the rev range: a cleaner pass when a gap opens and less need to change down when the road rises.
driving: Seven A roads are listed around Salisbury: the A36, A30, A338, A354, A345, A360 and A3094. The city lies near the edge of Salisbury Plain, and its neighbours are spread out, with Amesbury 9.8 km away, Tidworth 20 km and Romsey 24.2 km. In the 2021 Census, 8.9% of working residents of the Salisbury built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, about double the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. In 2025 MOT tests at SP postcode test stations, the Land Rover Discovery was the second most tested diesel car. With a trailer behind, a Discovery is the sort of vehicle where more mid-range torque from Stage 1 is noticed on every climb and overtake.

name: Scarborough
intro: It is 22.8 km in a straight line from Scarborough to Bridlington, 28 km to Driffield and 28.3 km to Whitby, so a trip to the next town is always a long one. Closer to home, the town rises steeply from its harbour, which means plenty of hill starts and climbs. Stage 1 remapping helps with both, through new fuel, boost and timing settings in the engine software, set within the engine's limits. On a diesel, stronger mid-range torque makes overtaking on a long A-road run easier and lets the engine take a steep street in a higher gear. Any change in fuel use is modest and depends on how the vehicle is driven.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 32.6% of households in the Scarborough built-up area had no car, against 25.9% across the Scarborough council area, and 5.8% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. No motorway appears among the main roads, which are the A64, A165, A171 and A170, and the three nearest service areas, Teesside Truck Stop on the A66, Exelby on the A19 and Bilbrough Top on the A64, are all more than 61 km away. At the end of June 2026, 33.2% of privately kept cars in the North Yorkshire council area were diesel, against 29.1% in England. With services that far apart, a diesel should be in good health before any remap, so faults are fixed first.

name: Scunthorpe
intro: In the year to June 2026, privately kept diesel cars in the North Lincolnshire council area went from 38,579 to 37,168, a fall of 3.7%, against 5.3% across England. Diesel still makes up 41.8% of private cars there, compared with 29.1% in England, so plenty of owners are holding on to theirs. For a diesel that is staying, Stage 1 remapping changes how the engine drives: it is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept inside the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. The gain you feel is mid-range torque, which helps with overtaking, joining the M180 and pulling a load. Insurers must be told about a remap.
driving: The M181 and A1077(M) are also on Scunthorpe's road list, with the A18, A159 and A1029, yet the nearest service area, Moto Doncaster (North) on the M180, is 22.7 km away in a straight line. Brough is 17.1 km off, Barton-upon-Humber 18 km and Goole 20.5 km. In the 2021 Census, 59.3% of working residents in the Scunthorpe built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 6.1% travelled 30 km or more, against 4.4%. In 2025 MOT tests across DN postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter and Ford Transit Custom were among the five most tested diesel vans. A loaded Sprinter on a long motorway run benefits from extra low-rev torque, within what its gearbox and clutch can take.

name: Sedgley
intro: Sedgley recorded 63.6% of working residents driving to work in its built-up area in the 2021 Census, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1% and above the 59% recorded across the Dudley council area. Yet only 1.9% travelled 30 km or more, so the daily drive was mostly a local one. That daily drive is where Stage 1 remapping would be judged. On a diesel, extra torque at everyday revs makes the car feel stronger pulling away and at town speeds, with fewer gear changes. Economy is a separate question: any change depends on how and where the car is driven, and on short runs it may be small. Your insurer also needs to know about the remap.
driving: Sedgley lies between Wolverhampton and Dudley, with Coseley 2.5 km away, Dudley 3.5 km and Wombourne 4.8 km. Its main roads include the A463, A449 and A4150, and the choice of motorway services is almost even, with Frankley on the M5 at 13.2 km and Hilton Park on the M6 at 13.9 km. The 2021 Census found two or more cars in 41.3% of Sedgley's households, above the England and Wales figure of 35.4%. Petrol cars made up 59.2% of those privately kept across the Dudley council area in June 2026, against 57.6% for England, and petrol engines can be remapped too. Fifth among diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across DY postcodes was the Ford Kuga, and a Kuga used for towing gains from extra low-rev torque.

name: Sevenoaks
intro: Sevenoaks differed sharply from its wider council area on driving to work in the 2021 Census: 26.9% of working residents in the built-up area drove, against 41.2% in the Sevenoaks council area and 45.1% for England and Wales. Census day fell in a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual, yet 6.2% still travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. If your car is not the daily commuter, Stage 1 remapping is judged on the trips it does make, such as a motorway run with a full boot or a caravan behind. The remap adjusts fuel, boost and timing in software, staying within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on.
driving: Two motorways, the M25 and M26, are on the Sevenoaks road list, along with the A21, A25, A224 and A225. RoadChef Clacket Lane on the M25 is the closest service area at 10.2 km, and Tollgate on the A2 is 19.7 km away. Bromley is 15 km from the town and Tonbridge 11.4 km. In the Sevenoaks council area, privately kept diesel cars fell from 14,832 to 13,617 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 8.2% against 5.3% across England, and petrol now accounts for 65% of private cars. On a diesel, the mid-range torque from a remap is what most drivers notice, above all when merging onto the M25 or pulling out to pass on the A21.

name: Sheffield

caz.name: Sheffield Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers Sheffield city centre and the inner ring road and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: Hills come with the territory in Sheffield, which sits in the Don valley at the foot of the Pennines. The council area also counted 14,682 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, and a loaded van on a climb is where Stage 1 remapping shows its value: more mid-range torque, fewer downshifts and easier pulling away with weight on board. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and the gearbox and clutch still set how far a van's remap can go. A van with an AdBlue, DPF or EGR fault is repaired first.
driving: Sheffield's Clean Air Zone, a Class C charging zone covering the city centre and inner ring road, charges vans but not private cars. A remap does not change a van's emissions standard, so the charge is unaffected. The M1 is among the main roads, with the A61, A57, A621 and A630, and the Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is just 3 km away. In the 2021 Census, 43.9% of working residents in the Sheffield built-up area drove to work and 30.6% of households had no car. Diesel was 32.6% of private cars in the council area and 95.3% of private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across S postcodes, the Ford Transit was by far the most tested diesel van, and the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus led the cars.

name: Shipley
intro: Shipley runs straight into Bradford as one built-up stretch, and Baildon is only 1.9 km away in a straight line, with Bradford at 4.3 km and Bingley at 4.8 km. With neighbours that close, many trips are short, so it is worth making sure the engine is healthy before any Stage 1 remapping: a vehicle with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first. The remap itself is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, inside the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. What you notice afterwards is mid-range torque, so the car pulls cleanly from low revs and needs fewer gear changes in slow traffic. Your insurer must be told about the remap.
driving: Seven postcode districts reach Shipley, from BD1 and BD2 out to BD17 and BD18. Car commuting there was lower than in the wider council area: in the 2021 Census, 41.8% of working residents in the Shipley built-up area drove to work, below the Bradford council area's 49.6% and the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. The council area also had fewer vans than England, with 63 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, against 81. Main roads include the A650, A6177, A658 and A657, and Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62 is 13.2 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across BD postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Audi A3 were the most tested diesel cars; on either, a remap mainly sharpens in-gear acceleration.

name: Shrewsbury
intro: Across the Shropshire council area there were 125 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, far above the England figure of 81. That means plenty of working vehicles on Shropshire's roads, and for a van in Shrewsbury, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about carrying weight. The remap works on software alone, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits. Extra mid-range torque helps a loaded van, or a pick-up with a trailer behind it, hold its speed on a long climb and change down less often. The gearbox and clutch have limits of their own, so a sensible van remap is set to stay inside them.
driving: No motorway appears on Shrewsbury's road list. The A5, A49, A53 and A458 carry the longer journeys, and the nearest service area is Nesscliffe on the A5, 13.3 km away. Towns are spread out: Telford is 18.9 km away and Oswestry 25.6 km. In the 2021 Census, 6.7% of working residents in the Shrewsbury built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. In 2025 MOT tests across SY postcodes, the Land Rover Discovery was the second most tested diesel car, and the Ford Ranger and Mitsubishi L200 both made the top five diesel vans. On a Discovery or a pick-up towing on the A49, Stage 1 gives firmer pull with the trailer on.

name: Sittingbourne
intro: Swale council area, which covers Sittingbourne, recorded a 32% diesel share of privately kept cars, above the England figure of 29.1% at the end of June 2026. The number of private diesel cars there fell by 4.5% over the year, a slower decline than England's 5.3%. With that many diesels still on the road, Stage 1 remapping has a practical audience. It is a change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, made in software and kept within the engine's limits. What diesel drivers notice is torque in the middle of the rev range: the car pulls harder from low speed, joins faster roads with less effort and holds a gear on a climb.
driving: Just three main roads are listed for Sittingbourne: the M2, the A249 and the A2. Moto Medway Services on the M2 is 9.2 km away. Faversham is 10.9 km off. In the 2021 Census, 24.9% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work and 6.9% went 30 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 19% and 4.4%, with census day in a lockdown. The Swale council area had 91 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, above England's 81. The Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van at ME postcode MOT stations in 2025, and a fully loaded Transit on the A249 is where a remap's extra torque matters most.

name: Skelmersdale
intro: Both the M58 and the M6 appear on Skelmersdale's road list, with the A577, A570 and A5068 among its A roads. Old Meadow Services on the M58 is 9.4 km away and Charnock Richard on the M6 10.7 km, so longer trips from the WN8 district are likely to include a motorway stretch. Stage 1 remapping on a diesel comes into its own on runs like that. It is applied with a remap file matched to the vehicle, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. The extra mid-range torque means fewer downshifts and less effort when overtaking. A car with a fault is repaired first.
driving: Car ownership in the Skelmersdale built-up area differs sharply from the wider council area. In the 2021 Census, 30.3% of households had no car, against 18% across the West Lancashire council area, and 28% had two or more, against 42.3%. Even so, 54.4% of working residents drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Orrell is 4.9 km away, Ormskirk 6.7 km and Wigan 8.8 km. Privately kept diesel cars in the West Lancashire council area fell by 6.1% in the year to June 2026. Among diesel cars given an MOT across WN postcodes in 2025, the Ford Focus and Nissan Qashqai were the two most tested. A remap on a Focus or Qashqai is about easier progress on the M58 and fewer gear changes around town.

name: Slough
intro: The M4, M40 and M25 are all on Slough's main road list, and ExtraMSA Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is about 8 km away. With three motorways nearby, many journeys can include a motorway stretch, and that is where a diesel's mid-range matters: joining from a slip road and pulling past slower traffic. A diesel with more mid-range torque pulls away from junctions more willingly, overtakes with less effort and holds a gear for longer. Nothing is fitted to the car: a remap file matched to the vehicle adjusts the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, within its limits. If the car has a fault with its DPF, AdBlue system or injectors, that is repaired first, and your insurer needs to know about the remap.
driving: The M53 is the only motorway among Wallasey's main roads, with the A5139, A554, A552, A5036, A41, A5227 and A565 making up the rest, and Old Meadow Services on the M58 is the nearest service area at 14.5 km. Work was closer to home than average in the 2021 Census: 15.5% of working residents in the Wallasey built-up area travelled 10 km or more, against 16.8% across the Wirral council area and 19% across England and Wales. At the end of June 2026 the council area had 70 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, below England's 81. In 2025 MOT tests across CH postcodes, the Ford Focus and Vauxhall Astra were among the most tested diesel cars. A remap leaves the emissions standard of cars like these unchanged.

name: Wallsend

Stage 1 remapping is a software job on fuel, boost and timing, done inside the engine's limits, so a diesel needs fewer downshifts when loaded and overtakes more calmly. Your insurer needs to hear about it.
driving: Wallsend sits at the eastern end of Hadrian's Wall, with Hebburn 3 km away, Longbenton 4.2 km and Jarrow 4.3 km. The A19, A1058, A187 and A193 are among its main roads, and Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is 10.3 km off, with Moto Washington on the A1(M) at 12.7 km. A Transporter carrying tools between nearby jobs gains low-rev pull from a Stage 1 remap, which shows most when it is fully loaded.

name: Waltham Forest
intro: Diesel cars are leaving Waltham Forest's roads more slowly than almost anywhere else we cover. A diesel that is staying on the road for a few more years is a fair candidate for Stage 1 remapping, provided it is healthy: any DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first. Fuel, boost and timing settings are then changed in software, within the engine's limits, and the gain is mid-range torque for overtaking and joining faster roads.
driving: Waltham Forest is inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily, and a remap won't change a vehicle's emissions standard or its ULEZ position. The M11, A12 and A406 are on the main road list, but the nearest listed service area, London Gateway Services on the M1, is 18.4 km away. Petrol made up 67.1% of the 70,139 private cars in June 2026 and petrol hybrids 11.4%. In 2025 MOT tests across E postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and BMW 5 Series led the diesel cars, and the Ford Transit the vans.

name: Walton-on-Thames
intro: Among the roads listed for Walton-on-Thames are the M3, the A3 and the A316, while Hersham is just 2.1 km away and the town itself sits on the south bank of the Thames. driving: Only 13.6% of households in the Walton-on-Thames built-up area were without a car in the 2021 Census, well under the 23.3% for England and Wales. In 2025 MOT tests across KT postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and Land Rover Discovery were the most tested diesel cars. For an E Class on a longer trip or a Discovery towing, Stage 1 brings stronger mid-range pull.

name: Wandsworth
intro: London's Ultra Low Emission Zone covers every London borough, Wandsworth included, and charges both cars and vans by the day. driving: The A3 and A24 are among the borough's main roads, with the A205, A214 and A217, and the nearest service area, Moto Heston on the M4, is 15.4 km away. In the 2021 Census, 47.9% of households in the Wandsworth council area had no car and 9.3% of working residents drove to work. Diesel cars fell from 10,084 to 9,511 over the year. Lambeth is 4.6 km away and Merton 4.8 km. For short trips across Inner London, a remap mainly makes a car feel more responsive when pulling away.

name: Warrington
intro: Diesel's decline has been sharp in Warrington. driving: The M62, M6 and M56 are all on Warrington's main road list, and Burtonwood Services on the M62 is about 5 km away, with Lymm Services on the M6 about 6 km. In the 2021 Census, 51.5% of working residents in the Warrington built-up area drove to work and 39.1% of households had two or more cars, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 35.4%. In 2025 MOT tests across WA postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car, narrowly ahead of the Ford Focus, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans. On motorway runs, the extra mid-range torque makes a loaded van easier to keep at pace, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Warwick
intro: Both the M40 and the A46 are on Warwick's list of main roads, along with the A425, A429 and A452. driving: The nearest service area, Warwick North (Budbrooke) on the A46, is only 2 km away, and Warwick Services on the M40 is 8.6 km. name: Waterlooville
intro: Compared with England and Wales as a whole, the Waterlooville built-up area leans heavily on the car. driving: The A3, A3(M), M27 and M275 are all on Waterlooville's road list. For a Qashqai or a 3 Series, a remap is felt as a stronger pull when joining the A3(M) and fewer downshifts on the way up to speed.

name: Watford
intro: Down 7.5% in a year: that is the fall in privately kept diesel cars in the Watford council area, from 9,150 to 8,468 in the year to June 2026, and one of the steepest drops among the 104 largest towns we cover.
